sections.title: FIN-M09-L05: Stocks and demat basics: ownership, costs and honest risks
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Explain what shares, demat and trading accounts are, what investing in single stocks costs and risks, and why most beginners lose money trading derivatives. **Time:** about 2 hours (30 minutes reading, 40 minutes resources, 50 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Shares and the market

A **share** is a small part of a company. When the company grows its profits over years, its share price tends to follow; when it struggles, the price falls, sometimes to nothing. Shares are bought and sold on stock exchanges (NSE and BSE) through a **SEBI-registered stockbroker**.

### The accounts you need

- **Demat account:** holds your shares and other securities electronically, with a depository participant. Your holdings appear in your consolidated account statement along with mutual funds ([AMFI CAS](https://www.amfiindia.com/investor-corner/investor-center/cas.html)).
- **Trading account:** with a broker, to place buy and sell orders.
- **Bank account** linked to both. Pay brokers only through official channels; registered brokers' UPI handles now use the "@valid" format with ".brk", and SEBI Check verifies them ([Moneylife](https://www.moneylife.in/article/sebi-launches-at-valid-upi-handles-and-checking-tool-to-curb-payment-frauds/78469.html)).

### Costs

Brokerage, securities transaction tax (STT), exchange and depository charges, stamp duty and GST on fees all reduce returns. Frequent trading multiplies them. Budget 2026 raised STT on futures from 0.02% to 0.05% and on options from 0.10% to 0.15% ([Outlook Money](https://www.outlookmoney.com/invest/union-budget-2026-buyback-proceeds-to-be-taxed-as-capital-gains-stt-raised-on-futures-and-options), check current rules).

### Tax, briefly

For listed shares (and equity funds): gains on shares held **12 months or less** are short-term and taxed at **20%**; longer holdings are long-term, taxed at **12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh a year** (sections 196 and 198 of the Income-tax Act, 2025) ([section 196](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-196-78), [section 198](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-198-78), check current rules). Dividends are added to your income. Module 10 covers the details.

### Single stocks: honest risks

- **Concentration:** one company can collapse through fraud, debt or competition. A few stocks are not a diversified portfolio.
- **Time and skill:** picking stocks well needs reading annual reports and understanding businesses, for years. Professionals with full-time teams often fail to beat the index.
- **Emotions:** watching prices daily leads to panic selling and greed buying (Module 1).

### Derivatives (F&O): the numbers

Futures and options are short-term bets on price moves, with leverage. SEBI's study of 2024-25 found that **about 91% of individual F&O traders lost money**, with net losses of **₹1,05,603 crore** in the year, about **₹1.1 lakh per person on average** ([Moneylife](https://moneylife.in/article/91-percentage-of-retail-traders-lost-money-in-derivatives-losses-in-fo-surged-41-percentage-to-rs105-lakh-crore-in-fy2425-sebi-study/77613.html)). Courses, Telegram groups and apps that promise daily income from "option trading" are selling you the 9% dream.

### Tips and "gurus"

Only SEBI-registered research analysts and investment advisers may recommend specific stocks for a fee ([SEBI](https://www.sebi.gov.in/media/press-releases/jun-2016/sebi-cautions-public-to-deal-with-only-sebi-registered-investment-advisers-and-research-analysts_32627.html)). SEBI's investor site warns about fake trading apps, "stock market guru" scams, pump-and-dump schemes and illegal dabba trading ([SEBI investor site](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/)). If a group shows screenshots of big profits and asks you to install an app or pay a fee, it is almost certainly a scam (Module 15).

### A sensible path

Many people start equity investing through **diversified index funds** (FIN-M09-L02), and treat direct stock investing, if at all, as a small, separate part of their long-term money that they research properly. Your Investment Policy Statement (Module 17) can set a limit, such as "single stocks: at most 10% of my equity".

## Local example

**Rahul's** office colleague, Suresh, joined a Telegram group called "Daily 5% Nifty Options Profit". The group shared screenshots of huge gains and offered a "premium plan" for ₹9,999. Suresh paid, followed the tips, and lost ₹62,000 in five weeks, including money from a personal loan.

Rahul shared SEBI's F&O study with him and checked the group's "analyst" on SEBI's registered intermediaries list: not registered. Suresh stopped trading and reported the group on the SEBI investor site's channels and the cyber crime portal.

Rahul wrote two rules in his own plan: "No F&O trading, ever, until I can explain why 91% lose," and "Any single stock buy must be researched for at least a month and stay under 10% of my equity money."

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Zerodha Varsity: all modules](https://zerodha.com/varsity/modules/) | Module 1, "Introduction to Stock Markets": the first five chapters | 40 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Moneylife: SEBI study, 91% of individual F&O traders lost money in 2024-25](https://moneylife.in/article/91-percentage-of-retail-traders-lost-money-in-derivatives-losses-in-fo-surged-41-percentage-to-rs105-lakh-crore-in-fy2425-sebi-study/77613.html) | SEBI's study of F&O losses in 2024-25 | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [SEBI investor website: guides and fraud warnings](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/) | The fraud warnings: fake trading apps, "stock market guru" scams, pump and dump, dabba trading | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Outlook Money: Budget 2026 changes buyback tax and STT on futures and options](https://www.outlookmoney.com/invest/union-budget-2026-buyback-proceeds-to-be-taxed-as-capital-gains-stt-raised-on-futures-and-options) | Budget 2026 changes to STT and buyback tax | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. If you have a demat account, log in and check: holdings, nominee, linked bank, and any unknown charges in the last statement. If you don't, write whether you need one now (most index-fund investors don't).
2. List every stock tip source you follow (groups, channels, apps). For each, check on SEBI's registered intermediaries list whether it is registered.
3. Leave or mute any unregistered tip source.
4. Write your stock rules for your Investment Policy Statement: whether you will hold single stocks, the maximum share of equity money, and your F&O rule.
5. Read one company's annual report summary (any listed company you use, such as a bank or a telecom company) and write three things you learned. This is practice in what "research" means.

**Proof to record:** Your demat check (or "not needed yet" note), your tip-source registration checks and your written stock rules, saved in 09 Investing.

## Template: stock rules (for your IPS)

```
Single stocks: Yes / Not now
If yes: at most ___% of my equity money; at most ___% in any one company
Research before buying: at least ___ weeks; I must be able to explain the business in 3 sentences
F&O: ____ (e.g. "No trading in futures and options")
Tips: I act only on SEBI-registered advisers I pay directly, after checking their registration
```

## Template: tip source check

```csv
Source (group, channel, app),Person or firm named,SEBI registration number shown?,Found on SEBI's list?,Promises returns?,Decision (leave / mute / keep)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Treating trading as investing.** Investing is owning good assets for years; trading is short-term betting with costs and taxes.
- **Following screenshot profits.** Losses are rarely posted. SEBI's data shows how most traders really do.
- **Buying a few "safe" stocks.** Even large companies can fall a lot. Diversify, or limit single stocks.
- **Paying for tips.** Only registered advisers and research analysts may give paid stock advice, and none can guarantee returns.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What share of individual F&O traders lost money in 2024-25, per SEBI's study?
    - A) About 91%
    - B) None
    - C) About 50%
    - D) About 10%
2. How are long-term gains on listed shares taxed, as of November 2026?
    - A) 1% of the sale value
    - B) 30% on all gains
    - C) Tax-free
    - D) 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh a year
3. What does a demat account do?
    - A) Files your tax return
    - B) Pays you interest
    - C) Lends you money
    - D) Holds your shares and securities electronically
4. A Telegram "guru" offers daily option-trading profits for a fee. What should you check first?
    - A) Nothing; just pay
    - B) Whether they are on SEBI's list of registered advisers or analysts
    - C) Their profit screenshots
    - D) Their follower count

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Varsity's introduction to stock markets, SEBI's F&O study, SEBI's fraud warnings and Budget 2026 STT changes
- **Action:** Check your demat (or decide you don't need one), check your tip sources' registration and write your stock rules. It is done when your proof is saved: your demat check (or "not needed yet" note), your tip-source registration checks and your written stock rules, saved in 09 Investing.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** Net losses were over ₹1 lakh crore that year.
2. **D.** Section 198 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (check current rules).
3. **D.** It is the electronic holding account; the trading account places orders.
4. **B.** Unregistered paid advice is illegal; most such groups are scams.

sections.title: FIN-M09-L06: Gold, REITs and real estate
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Compare ways to own gold, understand REITs, and judge a land or house purchase as an investment, with the costs, taxes and risks of each. **Time:** about 2 hours (30 minutes reading, 30 minutes resources, 60 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Gold: four ways to hold it

| Form | Good | Watch out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jewellery | Useful, culturally valued, can be pledged for a loan | Making charges and wastage you don't get back; purity questions; theft |
| Gold ETFs and gold mutual funds | Regulated by SEBI; no making charges; small amounts; easy to sell | Expense ratio; market price moves; ETFs need a demat account |
| Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) | Paid 2.5% a year interest on top of gold's price | No new issues since February 2024; the government said no further tranches ([Outlook Business, February 2025](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/economy-and-policy/govt-likely-to-discontinue-sovereign-gold-bond-schemes-confirms-finance-ministry)) |
| "Digital gold" on apps | Small amounts | SEBI warned in November 2025 that it operates outside SEBI's regulation, with no investor protection |

- **Hallmarking:** gold jewellery must carry a **6-digit HUID** (hallmark unique ID) since April 2023 ([GJEPC](https://gjepc.org/solitaire/?p=20069)), and the **BIS CARE app** lets you check a HUID ([Outlook Money](https://www.outlookmoney.com/invest/bought-gold-jewellery-recently-heres-how-you-can-check-its-purity-using-the-bis-care-app)). Check it before you buy.
- **SGBs you already hold:** RBI publishes dates for premature redemption (for example, a calendar for April to September 2026) ([RBI press release](https://website.rbi.org.in/web/rbi/-/press-releases/sovereign-gold-bond-sgb-scheme-calendar-for-premature-redemption-during-april-2026-september-2026)).
- **Digital gold:** SEBI's regulated alternatives are gold ETFs, electronic gold receipts and exchange-traded commodity derivatives ([Moneylife](https://moneylife.in/article/sebi-warns-against-investing-in-unregulated-digital-gold-and-egold-products/78789.html)).
- **Tax:** gold ETFs and funds count as long-term after 12 months (listed) at 12.5% ([AMFI tax corner](https://amfiindia.com/investor-corner/knowledge-center/tax-corner.html)); physical gold is long-term after 24 months ([Income Tax Department](https://incometaxindia.gov.in/Documents/Left%20Menu/income-from-capital-gains.htm)). Check current rules.

**How much gold?** Many people treat gold as a diversifier, a small share (often 5–10%) of long-term money, not the main investment. Kerala families often already hold a lot of gold as jewellery; count it before adding more.

### REITs

A **real estate investment trust (REIT)** owns income-producing commercial property, such as office parks, and pays most of its rental income to unitholders. REIT units trade on the stock exchange; SEBI cut the minimum application to **₹10,000–15,000** and the trading lot to **one unit** in 2021 ([Moneylife](https://www.moneylife.in/article/sebi-revises-minimum-application-value-trading-lot-for-reits-invits/64785.html), check current rules). Risks: vacancies, interest rates and market price swings. A REIT gives property exposure without buying a plot.

### Land and houses as investments

Real estate is the biggest store of wealth for many Kerala families. As an **investment** (not your own home, which is FIN-M11-L02):

- **Illiquid:** selling can take months or years, often at a discount when you need cash.
- **Big, single bets:** a plot concentrates wealth in one place.
- **Costs:** stamp duty and registration on buying, brokerage, maintenance and property tax every year.
- **Legal checks:** title deeds, encumbrance certificate, approvals. For projects, check registration with **K-RERA**, where you can search registered projects and file complaints ([K-RERA](https://rera.kerala.gov.in/)).
- **Returns:** rent is often a small percentage of the price; most of the hoped-for return is price growth, which varies a lot by place and time.
- **Tax:** long-term after 24 months at 12.5%; for land or buildings bought before 23 July 2024, resident individuals can pay 20% with indexation if that is lower ([section 197](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-197-78), check current rules).

Compare a plot's expected return honestly with alternatives, using the template, before borrowing for it.

## Local example

**Anu's** family planned to buy 5 cents of land near Kuttiady as "an investment for Anu's future", using a ₹4 lakh gold loan plus savings. Anu used the template with made-up but realistic numbers:

- Price ₹12 lakh, plus about ₹1 lakh for registration, stamp duty and brokerage.
- No rent (empty plot); yearly costs small.
- Hoped-for price in 8 years: ₹18 lakh. That is a yearly return of about 4.4% on ₹13 lakh, **before** the gold loan interest and before tax.

Meanwhile the gold loan would cost about 9% a year. The plot looked less like an investment and more like a bet on one location. The family decided not to borrow for it. Anu's father kept the idea of buying land later, with savings only, if a plot near family made sense for living, not as an investment.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Moneylife: SEBI warns against unregulated digital gold (November 2025)](https://moneylife.in/article/sebi-warns-against-investing-in-unregulated-digital-gold-and-egold-products/78789.html) | SEBI's warning on digital gold, and the regulated alternatives | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Outlook Business: no new Sovereign Gold Bond issues (February 2025)](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/economy-and-policy/govt-likely-to-discontinue-sovereign-gold-bond-schemes-confirms-finance-ministry) | Why there are no new Sovereign Gold Bond issues | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [GJEPC: hallmarked jewellery with a 6-digit HUID made mandatory from 1 April (2023)](https://gjepc.org/solitaire/?p=20069) | HUID hallmarking became mandatory (headline) | 2 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 (headline checked) |
| [Outlook Money: check gold jewellery purity with the BIS CARE app](https://www.outlookmoney.com/invest/bought-gold-jewellery-recently-heres-how-you-can-check-its-purity-using-the-bis-care-app) | Checking jewellery purity with the BIS CARE app (headline) | 2 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 (headline checked) |
| [Moneylife: REIT minimum investment cut, trading lot of one unit (August 2021)](https://www.moneylife.in/article/sebi-revises-minimum-application-value-trading-lot-for-reits-invits/64785.html) | REIT minimum investment and trading lot | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA)](https://rera.kerala.gov.in/) | K-RERA: search registered projects | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Income-tax Act, 2025, section 197: long-term gains on other assets](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-197-78) | Section 197: long-term gains on property and the pre-July 2024 option | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. List the gold your family holds (jewellery by weight, any ETFs, SGBs or "digital gold") and its approximate buyback value. Add your share to your Net Worth and Allocation tabs.
2. Check the HUID on one piece of jewellery with the BIS CARE app (if it was bought after April 2023).
3. If anyone holds "digital gold" on an app, write down what protection it has, using SEBI's warning.
4. Fill in the property investment check for any land or flat purchase your family is considering (or a made-up one).
5. Write your gold rule for your IPS: the maximum share of long-term money in gold and the forms you will use.

**Proof to record:** Your gold list, HUID check (or note), property investment check and gold rule, saved in 09 Investing.

## Template: property investment check

```
B2: purchase price (₹)
B3: buying costs (stamp duty, registration, brokerage) (₹)
B4: yearly rent received (₹)       B5: yearly costs (tax, upkeep) (₹)
B6: expected sale price (₹)        B7: years held
B8: total invested   =B2+B3
B9: yearly return %  =((B6+(B4-B5)*B7)/B8)^(1/B7)*100-100     (rough; ignores timing of rent)
B10: loan interest rate if borrowing (e.g. 9)
Is B9 well above B10 and above safe options? Yes / No
Legal checks: title [ ] encumbrance [ ] approvals [ ] K-RERA (for projects) [ ]
```

## Template: gold rule (for your IPS)

```
Gold as a share of my long-term money: at most ___%
Forms I use: ____ (e.g. gold ETF or gold fund; jewellery only for use)
I don't buy: ____ (e.g. unregulated digital gold)
Before buying jewellery: check HUID with BIS CARE
```

## Common mistakes

- **Counting jewellery as an investment at the buying price.** Making charges are gone the day you buy; value it at the buyback rate.
- **Buying "digital gold" as if it were regulated.** SEBI says it is outside its purview; use regulated forms.
- **Borrowing to buy land as an investment.** Loan interest is certain; land price growth is not.
- **Skipping legal checks.** Title problems can freeze property for years. Check documents and K-RERA registration.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What did SEBI say about "digital gold" products in November 2025?
    - A) They are the safest gold
    - B) They operate outside SEBI's regulation, with no investor protection
    - C) They pay 2.5% interest
    - D) They are government bonds
2. What is the HUID on gold jewellery?
    - A) A tax code
    - B) A bank account number
    - C) The shop's licence
    - D) A 6-digit hallmark ID you can check with the BIS CARE app
3. Are new Sovereign Gold Bonds being issued, as of November 2026?
    - A) Only for NRIs
    - B) Yes, every month
    - C) No; the last issue was in February 2024
    - D) Only in Kerala
4. What did SEBI change for REITs in 2021?
    - A) Minimum application cut to ₹10,000–15,000 and trading lot to one unit
    - B) Minimum raised to ₹1 crore
    - C) REITs were banned
    - D) REITs became tax-free

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** SEBI on digital gold, SGB status, HUID and BIS CARE, REIT rules, K-RERA and section 197
- **Action:** List your family's gold, check a HUID, run a property investment check and write your gold rule. It is done when your proof is saved: your gold list, HUID check (or note), property investment check and gold rule, saved in 09 Investing.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** SEBI pointed to gold ETFs, EGRs and exchange-traded derivatives as regulated options.
2. **D.** It identifies hallmarked jewellery; check it before buying.
3. **C.** The government said no further tranches would be issued.
4. **A.** This made REITs accessible to small investors.

sections.title: FIN-M09-L07: KSFE chitty, co-operative societies and crypto: benefits and risks
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Explain how a chitty works and its real cost or return, judge the safety of co-operative deposits, and state crypto's tax treatment and risks honestly. **Time:** about 2 hours (30 minutes reading, 30 minutes resources, 60 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### How a chitty works

A **chitty (kuri)** is a group saving-and-borrowing scheme. Each member pays a fixed instalment every month; each month one member gets the "prize", decided by auction. **KSFE**, owned by the Government of Kerala, runs chitties under the Central Chit Funds Act, 1982 ([KSFE](https://ksfe.com/chitty), check current rules):

- Tenures from **25 to 120 months**; instalments from **₹1,000 to ₹6,00,000 a month**.
- In each month's auction, the member who accepts the **biggest discount** on the chit amount wins the prize money. KSFE caps the discount at **30%, 35% or 40%**, depending on the chitty type.
- The discount, after the **foreman's commission** (the organiser's fee, stated in your chit agreement), is shared among members as a **dividend**, so everyone's instalment that month is lower.
- After winning, you must give **security** for the instalments still to come (a salaried person's surety, property, deposits, gold, insurance policies and others), or keep an equal amount in a KSFE deposit.

### Two roles, two costs

A chitty is a **loan** for early winners and a **saving** for late winners:

**Worked example** (illustrative numbers, not KSFE's): a ₹2,50,000 chitty of 50 months, 50 members, with net instalments averaging ₹4,250 after dividends.

- **Early winner:** bids the maximum discount in month 2 and receives ₹1,75,000, then keeps paying for the rest of the chitty. Total paid: about ₹2,12,500. The effective cost works out to about **11% a year**: like a loan.
- **Late winner:** waits until the last month and receives ₹2,37,500 (a small discount). The effective return is about **5.5% a year**: like a deposit.

Your real numbers depend on actual auction discounts, which you only know as the chitty runs. Use the template to calculate yours.

**Benefits:** forced monthly saving; access to a lump sum without a credit history; KSFE is government-owned. **Risks:** money is locked; you can't plan the auction outcome; borrowing through a chitty can be expensive; the security rules can delay your prize. **Private chit funds** that are unregistered or run informally carry real fraud risk. Never join one without checking its registration.

### Co-operative banks and societies

Kerala's co-operative sector serves millions of families, often with good service and slightly higher rates. Know what protects your money:

- **Co-operative banks registered with DICGC:** deposits insured up to **₹5 lakh per depositor per bank** ([DICGC](https://website.dicgc.org.in/sites/default/files/2024-09/DICGC_Flyer_0.pdf)).
- **Co-operative credit societies** that aren't licensed banks: RBI warned that some wrongly use the word "bank" and that **DICGC cover is not available** for their deposits ([RBI](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=52595)).
- **Kerala's own guarantee:** the Kerala Co-operative Deposit Guarantee (Amendment) Scheme, 2026 (notified 9 January 2026) provides a guarantee for **members'** deposits in societies, reported as up to **₹10 lakh per member**, depending on the society having paid its contribution to the fund ([TeamLease RegTech](https://www.teamleaseregtech.com/updates/article/51730/kerala-co-operative-deposit-guarantee-amendment-scheme-2026), [Indian Cooperative](https://www.indiancooperative.com/co-op-news-snippets/kerala-hikes-deposit-guarantee-for-co-op-members/), check current rules).
- Kerala has seen several co-operative and private finance failures. Spread deposits, stay within guarantee limits, and prefer institutions whose accounts and audit reports you can see.

### Crypto: not banned, not legal tender, heavily taxed

- **Legal status:** the government told Parliament in 2019 that India had **not banned** cryptocurrency and had no separate law for it ([Inc42, July 2019](https://inc42.com/?p=163021)); in 2022 the Finance Secretary said crypto "will never become legal tender": you can buy it, but it has no government authorisation and the government is not responsible for losses ([The Quint, February 2022](https://thequint.com/news/business/cryptocurrency-like-bitcoin-ethereum-nft-will-not-be-legal-tender-india-says-finance-secretary-tv-somanathan)). These are the latest official statements found for this course; check current rules, as crypto rules may change.
- **Tax:** income from transferring crypto (virtual digital assets) is taxed at a flat **30% plus surcharge and cess**, with **no deduction except the cost** of buying and **no set-off of losses** against other income; **1% TDS** applies on transfers above ₹50,000 a year (for most individuals) or ₹10,000 (others) ([Income Tax Department](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/20117/42998/Taxation-of-Virtual-Digital-Asset-VDA_2026-01-06_06-43-57_cfe04a_en.pdf/153706c8-7b5c-77d4-fc56-624c50ece1b0), check current rules).
- **Protection:** there is no investor-protection system for crypto like the ones for bank deposits or mutual funds. Exchanges can be hacked or shut; wrong transfers can't be reversed.
- **Scams:** fake crypto apps and "trading bots" that show rising balances you can't withdraw are among the most common investment frauds (Module 15).

If you choose to hold crypto, treat it as speculation: a small amount you could lose completely, outside your goals and emergency fund, and declared in your tax return.

## Local example

**Rahul** joined a ₹3,000-a-month KSFE chitty of 50 months (₹1,50,000), planning to use it for his sister's second-year fees. In month 9, he needed money and won the auction with a 28% discount: prize ₹1,08,000. He gave his salary certificate and a colleague's surety as security.

He calculated the real cost with the template: he had paid 9 instalments (averaging ₹2,600 after dividends), received ₹1,08,000, and would pay about 41 more instalments averaging ₹2,700. The effective cost came to about 19% a year, well above what a bank education loan would have cost, but he had no other quick option at the time. His lesson: "A chitty is a loan if you win early. Next time I'll compare it with a loan before I bid."

His mother, meanwhile, had ₹6 lakh in a primary co-operative society. They checked: it was not a licensed bank. They kept ₹3 lakh there (within the Kerala guarantee for members, after confirming her membership) and moved the rest to a post office MIS.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [KSFE: chitty](https://ksfe.com/chitty) | How KSFE chitties work: tenures, auctions, discounts, security | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [RBI: caution against co-operative societies using the word "bank" (November 2021)](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=52595) | Co-operative societies, the word "bank" and deposit insurance | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [TeamLease RegTech: Kerala Co-operative Deposit Guarantee (Amendment) Scheme, 2026](https://www.teamleaseregtech.com/updates/article/51730/kerala-co-operative-deposit-guarantee-amendment-scheme-2026) | The Kerala Co-operative Deposit Guarantee (Amendment) Scheme, 2026 | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Indian Cooperative: Kerala raises the co-op deposit guarantee to ₹10 lakh (January 2026)](https://www.indiancooperative.com/co-op-news-snippets/kerala-hikes-deposit-guarantee-for-co-op-members/) | The ₹10 lakh guarantee for co-op members (January 2026) | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Income Tax Department: taxation of virtual digital assets (PDF)](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/20117/42998/Taxation-of-Virtual-Digital-Asset-VDA_2026-01-06_06-43-57_cfe04a_en.pdf/153706c8-7b5c-77d4-fc56-624c50ece1b0) | How crypto (virtual digital assets) is taxed | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. List every chitty (KSFE or private) and co-operative deposit in your family: amount, institution, whether it is a licensed bank, and its insurance or guarantee.
2. For any chitty, fill in the chitty calculator with real or expected numbers and find whether it is working as a loan or a saving for you.
3. For private chitties, check the organiser's registration; if none, write a plan to stop at the next safe point.
4. For co-operative deposits, check: licensed bank or society? DICGC or Kerala guarantee? Within limits? Write one action if not.
5. Write your crypto rule for your IPS (for example, "none", or "at most 2% of long-term money, never borrowed").

**Proof to record:** Your chitty and co-operative list with protection checks, one chitty calculation (or the example) and your crypto rule, saved in 09 Investing.

## Template: chitty calculator (one row per month)

```
Row 1: Month,Instalment paid (₹, after dividend),Prize received (₹),Cash flow
D2: =C2-B2     (copy down for every month)
Monthly rate: =IRR(D2:D121)       Yearly rate %: =((1+IRR(D2:D121))^12-1)*100
If you won early, the yearly rate is your borrowing cost; compare with a bank loan.
If you won late, it is your saving return; compare with an RD or FD.
```

## Template: co-operative deposit check

```csv
Institution,Licensed bank or society?,DICGC insured?,Member? (for the Kerala guarantee),Amount (₹),Within ₹5 lakh (DICGC) or ₹10 lakh (Kerala guarantee)?,Audit report seen?,Action
```

## Common mistakes

- **Thinking a chitty is always a saving.** Win early and it is a loan, often an expensive one. Calculate both roles.
- **Joining unregistered chitties on trust.** Trust is not a guarantee. Check registration.
- **Putting large sums in one co-operative society.** Know which protection applies and stay within it.
- **Treating crypto as an investment for goals.** It is taxed heavily, unprotected and volatile. Keep it to money you can lose.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. In a chitty, who effectively borrows money?
    - A) Members who win the prize early
    - B) The government
    - C) Nobody
    - D) Members who win in the last month
2. What is KSFE's maximum chitty discount, per its website?
    - A) There is no limit
    - B) 100%
    - C) 30%, 35% or 40%, depending on the chitty type
    - D) 5%
3. Are deposits in a co-operative credit society that isn't a licensed bank covered by DICGC?
    - A) No
    - B) Yes, up to ₹5 lakh
    - C) Only for senior citizens
    - D) Yes, unlimited
4. How is income from selling crypto taxed, as of November 2026?
    - A) 12.5% after a year
    - B) Tax-free below ₹1 lakh
    - C) At your slab with all expenses deductible
    - D) 30% plus surcharge and cess, only cost deductible, no loss set-off

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** KSFE chitty rules, RBI on co-operative societies, the Kerala deposit guarantee scheme and crypto taxation
- **Action:** List and check your family's chitties and co-operative deposits, calculate one chitty and write your crypto rule. It is done when your proof is saved: your chitty and co-operative list with protection checks, one chitty calculation (or the example) and your crypto rule, saved in 09 Investing.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** They receive a discounted lump sum early and keep paying instalments.
2. **C.** The cap depends on the type of chitty (check current rules).
3. **A.** RBI says DICGC cover isn't available; Kerala's own guarantee scheme covers members' deposits within its limits.
4. **D.** Virtual digital assets have a special flat rate; 1% TDS applies on transfers above the limit.

sections.title: Module 10: Taxes
sections.summary: Understand income tax under the new Income-tax Act, 2025, choose the right regime with your own numbers, handle capital gains, TDS and advance tax, file your own return, and know the basics of tax and GST for freelancing and small business.
sections.content:
## Overview

Tax feels frightening mostly because it is unfamiliar. In this module you meet the new law (in force from 1 April 2026), build a calculator that applies both regimes' slabs, rebate, marginal relief and cess, open your Annual Information Statement to see what the department knows, and walk through filing a return step by step.

For a beginner on a modest income, the honest news is good: with the ₹12 lakh rebate in the new regime, many people pay no income tax at all, but filing still matters for TDS refunds and an income record. Freelancers and small business owners get presumptive taxation and the GST threshold explained, with links to the Entrepreneurship course for the business side. Your **tax checklist** is one of the eight parts of your final plan.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Explain income tax under the Income-tax Act, 2025: heads, slabs, rebate, cess, TDS and AIS
- Calculate tax under both regimes with a spreadsheet and choose your regime
- Work out capital gains tax and plan advance tax
- File and e-verify a return, knowing the due dates and late fees
- Apply presumptive taxation and the GST registration threshold to freelance or business income

## Time

About 12 hours in total: 10 hours 30 minutes of lessons and 1 hour 30 minutes for the module project. Part-time: weeks 20–22.

## Lessons

1. FIN-M10-L01: Income tax basics under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (about 2 hours)
2. FIN-M10-L02: Old regime or new? Worked examples and your own calculator (about 2 hours 30 minutes)
3. FIN-M10-L03: Capital gains, TDS and advance tax (about 2 hours)
4. FIN-M10-L04: File your own income tax return, step by step (about 2 hours)
5. FIN-M10-L05: Freelancers and small businesses: presumptive tax and GST basics (about 2 hours)

## Module project: My tax checklist and two-regime calculator

1. Check that your Tax tab has: income by head, the two-regime calculator (tested), and your regime decision for this year.
2. Complete your tax documents checklist and the ITR filing checklist.
3. Put the year's tax dates in your calendar: advance tax dates (if needed), the return due date and a reminder to check AIS before filing.
4. If you have freelance or business income, add your presumptive-tax comparison, invoice register and GST watch.
5. Write a one-paragraph tax plan: "This year I expect tax of ₹__ under the __ regime. TDS covers ₹__. I will pay __ by __, file by __, and keep records in __."

**Proof to record:** Your Tax tab, both checklists, calendar screenshot and one-paragraph tax plan, saved in 10 Tax.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basics | Can't explain TDS or AIS | Knows the terms | Checked own AIS and listed income by head |
| Regimes | Guesses | Compared roughly | Calculator built, tested and used for a decision |
| Gains and advance tax | Ignored | Knows the rates | Logged sales, totalled TDS, advance tax planned if needed |
| Filing | Never tried | Read the steps | Filed and e-verified, or completed a full dry run |
| Freelance and GST | Not considered | Knows the limits | Compared presumptive options and set up a GST watch (if relevant) |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Open your AIS and check TDS (FIN-M10-L01).
- Run your income through the two-regime calculator (FIN-M10-L02).
- Put the return due date and an AIS reminder in your calendar (FIN-M10-L04).

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| New Act in force from | 1 April 2026: the Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act. |
| New regime nil-tax limit with rebate | Total income up to ₹12 lakh (₹12.75 lakh salary with the ₹75,000 standard deduction). |
| Section 123 / 126 | The old 80C (₹1.5 lakh) and 80D (health insurance), old regime only. |
| Equity capital gains | Short-term (≤12 months) 20%; long-term 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh a year. |
| Advance tax dates | 15 June 15%, 15 September 45%, 15 December 75%, 15 March 100%; needed if tax after TDS ≥ ₹10,000. |
| e-Verification | Within 30 days of filing, or the return is invalid. |
| Due dates | 31 July (no business income), 31 August (business without audit), 31 October (audit). |
| Presumptive taxation | Business: 6% digital + 8% other receipts; specified professions: 50% of receipts (or actual if higher). |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Avoiding tax because it is confusing.** Late filing costs fees and refunds. Start with AIS and the calculator; it gets easier every year.
- **Letting tax decide investments.** Invest for goals; choose the regime afterwards by calculation.
- **Trusting messages about refunds or notices.** Everything real appears on the e-filing portal when you log in yourself.

sections.title: FIN-M10-L01: Income tax basics under the Income-tax Act, 2025
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Explain how income tax works in India under the new law: tax year, heads of income, slabs, rebate, cess, TDS, and where to see what the department already knows about you. **Time:** about 2 hours (30 minutes reading, 40 minutes resources, 50 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### A new law from 1 April 2026

The **Income-tax Act, 2025** came into force on **1 April 2026**, replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961 ([Income Tax Department](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/income-tax-act-2025-comes-into-force-from-1st-april-2026)). The government says the aim was to simplify the language and structure "without altering the underlying tax policy" ([CBDT press release](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/press-release-income-tax-act-2025-comes-into-force-from-01-april-2026-pdf)). So most rules you hear about still exist, under **new section numbers**. This course gives the new numbers with the old names in brackets, such as "section 123 (the old 80C)".

Returns filed during 2026 were for income earned in 2025-26 under the old law; your return for income earned from April 2026 onwards is under the new law. Form names and numbers may also change; the e-filing portal guides you.

### The basic idea

1. **Add up your income for the tax year** (1 April to 31 March) under five heads: **salary**, **house property**, **business or profession**, **capital gains**, and **other sources** (interest, dividends, gifts above limits and so on).
2. **Subtract the deductions your regime allows** to get **total (taxable) income**.
3. **Apply the slab rates** of your regime (FIN-M10-L02).
4. **Subtract any rebate**, then add **4% health and education cess** (and surcharge only on very high incomes) ([tax rates page](https://incometaxindia.gov.in/Documents/Left%20Menu/TAX%20RATES_Indvl.htm)).
5. **Subtract tax already paid**: TDS, advance tax. The rest is payable; if you paid too much, you get a refund.

### The two regimes, in one line each

- **New regime** (the default): lower slab rates, very few deductions. With the **rebate under section 156**, resident individuals with total income up to **₹12 lakh** pay **no tax** ([section 156](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-156-88)); salaried people also get a **₹75,000 standard deduction** ([section 19](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-19-206)).
- **Old regime:** higher slab rates, but deductions such as section 123 (the old 80C) and health insurance (section 126, the old 80D).

Budget 2026 kept the slabs, the ₹12 lakh rebate and the ₹75,000 standard deduction unchanged ([Storyboard18](https://www.storyboard18.com/special-coverage/budget-2026-no-change-in-tax-rates-in-budget-2026-rebate-continues-for-income-up-to-%e2%82%b912-lakh-88610.htm)). FIN-M10-L02 calculates both for you.

### TDS: tax deducted before you are paid

Employers deduct tax from salaries; banks deduct TDS on interest above a yearly limit; clients may deduct TDS from professional fees. **TDS is not an extra tax**: it is part of your tax, paid in advance. When you file, you add up your real tax, subtract all TDS, and pay the balance or get a refund. If you have no taxable income but TDS was deducted, **filing a return is how you get it back**.

### What the department already knows: AIS

The **Annual Information Statement (AIS)** on the e-filing portal shows what has been reported about you: TDS and TCS, specified financial transactions (such as large deposits or investments), tax payments, demands and refunds. Log in to the e-filing portal, go to **Services → Annual Information Statement (AIS)**, choose the year and open it; the **TIS** is a category-wise summary, and you can give feedback if something is wrong ([Income Tax Department](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/steps-to-access-ais-information-online)). Checking AIS before filing prevents most mismatch notices.

### Do you need to file?

You must file if your income is above the basic exemption limit, and in certain other situations defined in the law. Even if you don't have to, filing is useful: it claims TDS refunds, creates a record of income for loans and visas, and lets you carry forward some losses. The e-filing portal explains who must file.

## Local example

**Anu** had never filed a return: "My income is below the limit, so tax isn't for me." Then she logged in to the e-filing portal with her PAN for the first time and opened her AIS.

It showed ₹2,840 of TDS: a coaching centre where she had taught weekend classes had deducted TDS from her fees, and her bank had reported FD interest. Her total income for the year was about ₹1,90,000, far below the taxable limit, so her tax was ₹0. The only way to get the ₹2,840 back was to file a return.

She also saw the coaching centre had reported her fees under her PAN, so the department knew about that income. "AIS is the department's diary about me," she wrote. "I'll read it every year before filing." She files her first return in FIN-M10-L04.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [CBDT press release: the Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces the 1961 Act (PDF)](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/press-release-income-tax-act-2025-comes-into-force-from-01-april-2026-pdf) | The CBDT press release on the new Act: what changed and what didn't | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Income-tax Act, 2025, section 156: rebate](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-156-88) | Section 156: the rebate, in the new Act's own words | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Income Tax Department: steps to access your Annual Information Statement (AIS)](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/steps-to-access-ais-information-online) | Steps to open your AIS and TIS | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Zerodha Varsity: all modules](https://zerodha.com/varsity/modules/) | Module 7, "Markets and Taxation": the first chapters on how income is classified and taxed | 30 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Check that your PAN is active and linked to Aadhaar (the e-filing portal shows the status on login or under your profile). Register on the portal if you haven't.
2. Open your AIS and TIS for the latest year available. Note every item: TDS, interest, dividends, transactions.
3. Check each item against your own records. Note anything wrong for feedback.
4. Make a **Tax** tab and list your income for the current tax year by the five heads, even if it is small.
5. Start your tax documents list using the template: what you have, what you need to collect.

**Proof to record:** A screenshot of your AIS summary (PAN and account numbers covered), your income by head and your documents list, saved in 10 Tax.

## Template: income by head (Tax tab)

```csv
Head,Source,Amount for the tax year (₹),Proof or document,TDS deducted (₹)
Salary,,,(salary slips / employer's TDS certificate),
House property,,,,
Business or profession,(tuition, freelance fees),,(invoices, bank statement),
Capital gains,(sales of funds, shares, gold, land),,(CAS, broker statement),
Other sources,(savings and FD interest, dividends),,(bank interest certificate),
Total,,=SUM(C2:C6),,=SUM(E2:E6)
```

## Template: tax documents checklist

```
[ ] PAN active and linked to Aadhaar
[ ] e-filing portal login works; bank account pre-validated for refunds
[ ] Salary slips and employer's TDS certificate (if salaried)
[ ] Bank interest certificates for every account and FD
[ ] Mutual fund and demat capital gains statements (CAS, broker report)
[ ] Rent receipts, insurance premium receipts, PPF/ELSS/NPS proofs (only if using the old regime)
[ ] AIS and TIS downloaded and checked
[ ] Invoices and receipts register (freelance or business income)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Thinking "no tax due" means "no return needed".** Filing claims TDS refunds and builds an income record. Check whether you must file.
- **Ignoring AIS.** Mismatches between your return and AIS cause notices. Check it before filing.
- **Treating TDS as the final tax.** TDS is an advance. Your real tax may be more (pay the rest) or less (claim a refund).
- **Using old section numbers in new-law forms.** The rules mostly carried over, but numbers changed. Use the new Act's numbers for tax years from April 2026.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. From when is the Income-tax Act, 2025 in force?
    - A) 1 January 2027
    - B) It hasn't started
    - C) 1 April 2026
    - D) 1 April 2025
2. Under the new regime, up to what total income does a resident individual pay no tax because of the rebate?
    - A) ₹7 lakh
    - B) ₹2.5 lakh
    - C) ₹5 lakh
    - D) ₹12 lakh
3. Your bank deducted ₹2,000 TDS but your income is below the taxable limit. How do you get it back?
    - A) It can't be recovered
    - B) Ask the bank branch for cash
    - C) Apply to RBI
    - D) File an income tax return
4. Where can you see what TDS and transactions have been reported under your PAN?
    - A) Your passbook only
    - B) Form 15G
    - C) Your credit report
    - D) The Annual Information Statement (AIS) on the e-filing portal

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The CBDT press release, section 156, the AIS steps and Varsity's taxation basics
- **Action:** Check your PAN and AIS, list your income by head and start your tax documents checklist. It is done when your proof is saved: a screenshot of your AIS summary (PAN and account numbers covered), your income by head and your documents list, saved in 10 Tax.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** It replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026.
2. **D.** Section 156 gives a rebate of up to ₹60,000, so tax is nil up to ₹12 lakh of total income.
3. **D.** TDS credits are refunded through the return.
4. **D.** AIS shows TDS/TCS, specified transactions, tax paid, demands and refunds.

sections.title: FIN-M10-L02: Old regime or new? Worked examples and your own calculator
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Calculate income tax under both regimes for sample incomes and your own, with a spreadsheet that applies slabs, rebate, marginal relief and cess, and choose the right regime. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (30 minutes reading, 30 minutes resources, 90 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### New regime (section 202, the default)

| Total income | Rate |
| --- | --- |
| Up to ₹4,00,000 | Nil |
| ₹4,00,001 – ₹8,00,000 | 5% |
| ₹8,00,001 – ₹12,00,000 | 10% |
| ₹12,00,001 – ₹16,00,000 | 15% |
| ₹16,00,001 – ₹20,00,000 | 20% |
| ₹20,00,001 – ₹24,00,000 | 25% |
| Above ₹24,00,000 | 30% |

([section 202](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-202-78), check current rules.) Salaried people deduct a **₹75,000 standard deduction** first. The **rebate** makes tax nil up to ₹12 lakh of total income; just above ₹12 lakh, **marginal relief** limits the tax to the income above ₹12 lakh, so a small rise in income never costs more than the rise itself ([section 156](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-156-88)). Add 4% cess. Most other deductions aren't allowed; employer contributions to NPS are an important exception (FIN-M09-L04).

### Old regime

| Total income (below 60) | Rate |
| --- | --- |
| Up to ₹2,50,000 | Nil |
| ₹2,50,001 – ₹5,00,000 | 5% |
| ₹5,00,001 – ₹10,00,000 | 20% |
| Above ₹10,00,000 | 30% |

For residents aged 60 to 80 the nil band is ₹3 lakh, and for 80+ ₹5 lakh ([tax rates](https://incometaxindia.gov.in/Documents/Left%20Menu/TAX%20RATES_Indvl.htm)). The rebate makes tax nil up to ₹5 lakh of total income. The standard deduction is ₹50,000. The main deductions:

- **Section 123 (the old 80C), up to ₹1.5 lakh:** EPF and PPF contributions, life insurance premiums, ELSS, NSC, 5-year tax-saving deposits, SCSS, tuition fees for two children, home loan principal, and stamp duty on a house ([Schedule XV](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/schedule-xv-2), [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/finance/personal-finance/i-t-bill-2025-deductions-under-80c-moves-to-section-123-see-changes-125021700699_1.html)).
- **Section 126 (the old 80D):** health insurance, ₹25,000 for self and family and ₹25,000 for parents, ₹50,000 each for senior citizens ([section 126](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-126-96)).
- **NPS:** an extra ₹50,000 (the old 80CCD(1B)).
- Others with conditions: home loan interest, house rent allowance, professional tax, education loan interest.

### Who should choose which?

Your employer may ask you at the start of the year, for TDS. Individuals **without business income** can choose the regime **every year** when filing; those **with business or professional income** opt out of the new regime by the due date, and can switch back only once (section 202(4)) ([section 202](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-202-78)).

### Worked examples (salaried, under 60, tax year 2026-27 rates)

Old-regime deductions assumed: standard ₹50,000 + section 123 ₹1,50,000 + health insurance ₹25,000 + professional tax ₹2,500 = **₹2,27,500**. Tax includes 4% cess; surcharge ignored.

| Salary | New: taxable | New: tax | Old: taxable | Old: tax | Lower | Old wins only if deductions exceed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ₹6,00,000 | ₹5,25,000 | ₹0 | ₹3,72,500 | ₹0 | Same | Old can't beat ₹0 |
| ₹9,00,000 | ₹8,25,000 | ₹0 | ₹6,72,500 | ₹48,880 | New | Old can't beat ₹0 |
| ₹13,00,000 | ₹12,25,000 | ₹26,000 | ₹10,72,500 | ₹1,39,620 | New | ₹7,37,500 |
| ₹18,00,000 | ₹17,25,000 | ₹1,50,800 | ₹15,72,500 | ₹2,95,620 | New | ₹6,91,667 |

The pattern: **with the ₹12 lakh rebate, the new regime wins for most people** unless they have very large deductions (a big home loan interest, high rent with HRA, full section 123 and NPS). At ₹18 lakh, the old regime wins only if total deductions (including the standard deduction) exceed about ₹6,91,667.

### Do the calculation, don't guess

Your own numbers decide. The template builds both regimes with formulas, so you can test different deductions and see the break-even. Then cross-check your result with the Income Tax Department's own **income and tax calculator**, which compares the regimes for a chosen year, age and income ([official calculator](https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/income-tax-calculator)). Revisit it every year: rules, your income and your deductions all change.

## Local example

**Rahul's** salary for the tax year is ₹4,20,000 (made-up). His office asked him to choose a regime for TDS.

- **New:** ₹4,20,000 − ₹75,000 = ₹3,45,000 taxable, below ₹4 lakh: **tax ₹0**.
- **Old:** he could claim his NPS contribution, his mother's money-back premium for him and Medisep (Module 14), but with income this low the old regime also gives **₹0** after the rebate.

Both are zero, so he chose the default new regime, which is simpler. He then played with the calculator for his future: at a salary of ₹13 lakh with his likely deductions, the new regime would cost ₹26,000 and the old ₹1,39,620. "I don't need to buy anything just to save tax," he noted. "I'll invest for my goals and let the regime follow the numbers."

**Fathima** (freelancer) has business income, so she can't switch freely every year: once she opts for the old regime she can come back to the new one only once. She decided to stay in the new regime unless her calculator shows a clear, lasting advantage.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Income-tax Act, 2025, section 202: new tax regime rates](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-202-78) | Section 202: new regime slabs and the rules for opting out | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Income-tax Act, 2025, section 156: rebate](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-156-88) | Section 156: rebate and marginal relief | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Income-tax Act, 2025, section 19: deductions from salary](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-19-206) | Section 19: standard deduction and professional tax | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Income Tax Department: tax rates for individuals (old regime, surcharge, cess)](https://incometaxindia.gov.in/Documents/Left%20Menu/TAX%20RATES_Indvl.htm) | Old regime slabs, senior citizen limits, surcharge and cess | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Income-tax Act, 2025, Schedule XV: what counts for the section 123 (old 80C) deduction](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/schedule-xv-2) | Schedule XV: what counts for section 123 (old 80C) | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Income-tax Act, 2025, section 126: health insurance deduction (old 80D)](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-126-96) | Section 126: the health insurance deduction | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Income Tax Department: income and tax calculator (compares regimes)](https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/income-tax-calculator) | The official income and tax calculator: try the basic calculator with your income | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Build the two-regime calculator in your Tax tab from the template.
2. Test it with the four worked examples in this lesson; your answers must match the table.
3. Enter your own expected income for this tax year (salary, freelance, interest), and the deductions you really have (not ones you might buy).
4. Read the result and the break-even: how much in deductions would make the old regime worth it?
5. Cross-check your own case on the Income Tax Department's official income and tax calculator; if the answers differ, find out why (age, year or a deduction).
6. Write your regime decision for this year and one sentence on why. If you have business income, note the switching rule.

**Proof to record:** A screenshot of your Tax tab calculator showing the four test cases matching and your own result with your regime decision, saved in 10 Tax.

## Template: two-regime calculator (Tax tab)

```
INPUTS
B2: salary income (₹)                 B3: other income (interest, freelance profit, etc.) (₹)
B4: salaried? (1 = yes, 0 = no)       B5: old-regime deductions excluding standard deduction (₹)

NEW REGIME
B8: taxable        =MAX(B2+B3-75000*B4,0)
Slab table in D8:E14  (lower limit | extra rate):  0|0  400000|0.05  800000|0.05  1200000|0.05  1600000|0.05  2000000|0.05  2400000|0.05
B9: slab tax       =SUMPRODUCT((B8>D8:D14)*(B8-D8:D14)*E8:E14)
B10: after rebate  =IF(B8<=1200000,0,MIN(B9,B8-1200000))
B11: with 4% cess  =ROUND(B10*1.04,0)

OLD REGIME
B14: taxable       =MAX(B2+B3-50000*B4-B5,0)
Slab table in D17:E20 (lower limit | extra rate):  0|0  250000|0.05  500000|0.15  1000000|0.10
B15: slab tax      =SUMPRODUCT((B14>D17:D20)*(B14-D17:D20)*E17:E20)
B16: after rebate  =IF(B14<=500000,0,B15)
B17: with 4% cess  =ROUND(B16*1.04,0)

B20: lower regime  =IF(B11<B17,"New",IF(B17<B11,"Old","Same"))
B21: difference    =ABS(B11-B17)
Notes: surcharge (above ₹50 lakh) is not included. Seniors: change 250000 to 300000 (60-80) or 500000 (80+) in D18.
```

## Common mistakes

- **Choosing the old regime out of habit.** Since the ₹12 lakh rebate, the new regime often wins. Calculate both every year.
- **Buying products just to save tax.** An endowment policy or ELSS bought only for the deduction can cost more than the tax saved.
- **Forgetting cess.** Add 4% to the tax. Small, but it should be in your plan.
- **Switching freely with business income.** With business or professional income you can return to the new regime only once.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Salary ₹9 lakh, new regime: what is the tax?
    - A) ₹25,000
    - B) ₹0
    - C) ₹90,000
    - D) ₹45,000
2. In the old regime, what is the section 123 (old 80C) limit?
    - A) ₹1.5 lakh
    - B) ₹2.5 lakh
    - C) No limit
    - D) ₹50,000
3. Taxable income in the new regime is ₹12,25,000. What does marginal relief limit the tax to (before cess)?
    - A) ₹0
    - B) ₹25,000
    - C) ₹63,750
    - D) ₹1,22,500
4. A salaried person with no business income: how often can they choose the regime?
    - A) Every month
    - B) Once in a lifetime
    - C) Every year, when filing
    - D) Never; the employer decides
5. Which formula applies new-regime slabs from a slab table?
    - A) =VLOOKUP(B8,D8:E14,2)*B8
    - B) =B8*0.3
    - C) =SUM(D8:D14)
    - D) =SUMPRODUCT((B8>D8:D14)*(B8-D8:D14)*E8:E14)

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Sections 202, 156 and 19, the old regime rates page, Schedule XV and section 126
- **Action:** Build the two-regime calculator, test it against the worked examples and choose your regime with your own numbers. It is done when your proof is saved: a screenshot of your Tax tab calculator showing the four test cases matching and your own result with your regime decision, saved in 10 Tax.
- **Quiz:** at least 4 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** ₹9,00,000 − ₹75,000 = ₹8,25,000, below ₹12 lakh, so the rebate makes it nil.
2. **A.** The limit carried over unchanged into the new Act.
3. **B.** Tax can't exceed the income above ₹12 lakh: ₹25,000.
4. **C.** Only those with business income face the one-time switch-back rule.
5. **D.** It adds each slab's extra rate on the income above that slab's lower limit.

sections.title: FIN-M10-L03: Capital gains, TDS and advance tax
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Work out the tax on selling investments, gold or property, track TDS through the year, and pay advance tax on time if you need to. **Time:** about 2 hours (30 minutes reading, 30 minutes resources, 60 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Capital gains: what you pay when you sell

**Capital gain = sale price − purchase cost (and allowed expenses)**. Whether it is short-term or long-term depends on how long you held the asset. As of November 2026 (check current rules):

| Asset | Long-term after | Short-term tax | Long-term tax |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Listed shares, equity mutual funds (STT paid) | 12 months | 20% (section 196) | 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh a year (section 198) |
| Debt mutual funds bought from 1 April 2023 | Never: always short-term | Your slab rate (section 76) | — |
| Gold ETFs and other listed funds | 12 months | Your slab rate | 12.5% |
| Physical gold, land, buildings, unlisted assets | 24 months | Your slab rate | 12.5%; for land or buildings bought before 23 July 2024, residents can choose 20% with indexation if lower (section 197) |
| Crypto (virtual digital assets) | — | 30% flat on gains; no loss set-off | 30% flat |

Sources: [section 196](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-196-78), [section 198](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-198-78), [section 76](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-76-106), [section 197](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-197-78), [holding periods](https://incometaxindia.gov.in/Documents/Left%20Menu/income-from-capital-gains.htm), [AMFI tax corner](https://amfiindia.com/investor-corner/knowledge-center/tax-corner.html), [VDA taxation](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/20117/42998/Taxation-of-Virtual-Digital-Asset-VDA_2026-01-06_06-43-57_cfe04a_en.pdf/153706c8-7b5c-77d4-fc56-624c50ece1b0). From Budget 2026, money received in a company **buyback** is also taxed as capital gains ([Outlook Money](https://www.outlookmoney.com/invest/union-budget-2026-buyback-proceeds-to-be-taxed-as-capital-gains-stt-raised-on-futures-and-options)).

**Worked example:** Fathima sells equity index fund units after 3 years, with a gain of ₹1,60,000. Long-term gains up to ₹1,25,000 a year are tax-free; tax is 12.5% of ₹35,000 = ₹4,375, plus 4% cess = **₹4,550**. Had she sold after 10 months, the whole ₹1,60,000 would be short-term: 20% = ₹32,000 plus cess.

Some long-term investors **use the ₹1.25 lakh yearly exemption** by selling and buying back units to raise their cost; it is legal, but check exit loads and costs, and keep records.

### TDS through the year

- **Salary:** your employer estimates your yearly tax under your chosen regime and deducts it monthly. Tell your employer about other income if you want TDS to cover it.
- **Interest:** banks deduct TDS when interest from that bank crosses a yearly limit, ₹50,000 for most people and higher for senior citizens ([Finance Bill 2026 notes](https://incometaxindia.gov.in/Budgets%20and%20Bills/2026/Notes-on-clauses-2026.pdf)); if your total income is below the taxable limit, you can give the bank a self-declaration so it doesn't deduct.
- **Dividends and professional fees:** fund houses, companies and business clients may deduct TDS above small yearly limits.

All TDS shows in your AIS. Check it every quarter.

### Advance tax: paying as you earn

If your tax for the year, **after TDS**, will be **₹10,000 or more**, you pay it in instalments during the year, under sections 403 to 405 of the new Act ([Sansa Legal, June 2026](https://www.sansalegal.com/post/advance-tax-under-income-tax-act-2025-due-dates-calculation-and-payment-guide), check current rules):

| By | Cumulative share of your estimated tax |
| --- | --- |
| 15 June | 15% |
| 15 September | 45% |
| 15 December | 75% |
| 15 March | 100% |

- People using **presumptive taxation** (FIN-M10-L05) can pay all of it by **15 March**.
- **Resident senior citizens without business income** don't have to pay advance tax.
- Late or short payment means interest. Most salaried people don't need advance tax, because TDS covers it; freelancers often do.

Pay through the e-filing portal's **e-Pay Tax** service, and keep the challan details.

## Local example

**Fathima** estimated her tax for the year: about ₹38,000, with ₹6,000 already deducted as TDS by two Indian clients. The balance, ₹32,000, is above ₹10,000, so she needs advance tax.

Is she under presumptive taxation (FIN-M10-L05)? Yes, so she can pay it all by 15 March. But to avoid a big bill at once, she set up the planner anyway: ₹4,800 by 15 June, ₹14,400 by 15 September, ₹24,000 by 15 December, and the rest by 15 March, from the tax reserve in her holding account (FIN-M03-L04).

She also checked her AIS in October and found one client's TDS missing. She emailed the client, who had quoted her PAN wrongly; it was corrected before she filed.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Income-tax Act, 2025, section 196: short-term gains on equity](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-196-78) | Section 196: short-term gains on equity | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Income-tax Act, 2025, section 198: long-term gains on equity](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-198-78) | Section 198: long-term gains on equity and the ₹1.25 lakh exemption | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Income-tax Act, 2025, section 197: long-term gains on other assets](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-197-78) | Section 197: long-term gains on property and other assets | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [AMFI: tax corner (how mutual funds are taxed)](https://amfiindia.com/investor-corner/knowledge-center/tax-corner.html) | AMFI's tax corner: how each type of fund is taxed | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Sansa Legal: advance tax under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (June 2026)](https://www.sansalegal.com/post/advance-tax-under-income-tax-act-2025-due-dates-calculation-and-payment-guide) | Advance tax under the new Act: who, when, how much | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Zerodha Varsity: all modules](https://zerodha.com/varsity/modules/) | Module 7, "Markets and Taxation": the chapters on capital gains | 20 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. If you sold any investment, gold or property this tax year (or last), fill in the capital gains log for it and calculate the tax.
2. Estimate your total tax for this tax year using your Tax tab calculator.
3. Add up the TDS deducted so far (from AIS) and expected for the rest of the year.
4. If tax after TDS is ₹10,000 or more, fill in the advance tax planner and put the four dates in your calendar.
5. If you have FD interest and no taxable income, ask your bank for the self-declaration form so TDS isn't deducted.

**Proof to record:** Your capital gains log (or "no sales"), your TDS total from AIS and your advance tax planner or a note that you don't need one, saved in 10 Tax.

## Template: capital gains log

```
Asset,Bought on,Sold on,Months held,Cost (₹),Sale value (₹),Gain (₹),Short or long?,Rate,Tax (₹)
D2: =DATEDIF(B2,C2,"M")     G2: =F2-E2
Equity long-term tax (after the ₹1.25 lakh yearly exemption, for all equity gains together):
=MAX(SUM(equity long-term gains)-125000,0)*0.125*1.04
```

## Template: advance tax planner

```
Estimated tax for the year (₹):          B2
TDS expected for the year (₹):           B3
Tax after TDS:                           B4 =B2-B3     Need advance tax? =IF(B4>=10000,"Yes","No")
By 15 June (15%):                        =B4*0.15
By 15 September (45% total):             =B4*0.45
By 15 December (75% total):              =B4*0.75
By 15 March (100%):                      =B4
Paid so far (challan dates and amounts): ____
```

## Common mistakes

- **Selling equity just before 12 months.** A few weeks can change the rate from 20% to 12.5% with a ₹1.25 lakh exemption. Check the date.
- **Thinking debt funds still get long-term rates.** Units bought from April 2023 are taxed at your slab, however long you hold them.
- **Ignoring advance tax as a freelancer.** Interest for late payment adds up. Use your tax reserve and the planner.
- **Not checking AIS for TDS.** Missing or wrong TDS entries cost you money unless corrected before filing.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. You sell equity fund units held 3 years with a ₹2,25,000 gain (no other gains). Tax before cess?
    - A) ₹45,000
    - B) ₹28,125
    - C) ₹0
    - D) ₹12,500
2. When are listed equity shares long-term, as of November 2026?
    - A) After 36 months
    - B) Never
    - C) After 12 months
    - D) After 24 months
3. Your tax after TDS for the year is ₹8,000. Do you need advance tax?
    - A) No; the threshold is ₹10,000
    - B) Yes, always
    - C) Only in March
    - D) Only if salaried
4. By 15 September, how much of your estimated tax should be paid in total?
    - A) 45%
    - B) 15%
    - C) 75%
    - D) 100%

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Sections 196, 197 and 198, AMFI's tax corner, the advance tax rules and Varsity's capital gains chapters
- **Action:** Log any capital gains, total your TDS from AIS and plan advance tax if you need it. It is done when your proof is saved: your capital gains log (or "no sales"), your TDS total from AIS and your advance tax planner or a note that you don't need one, saved in 10 Tax.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** (₹2,25,000 − ₹1,25,000) × 12.5% = ₹12,500.
2. **C.** Listed securities and equity-oriented funds: more than 12 months.
3. **A.** Advance tax applies when tax after TDS is ₹10,000 or more.
4. **A.** 15% by June, 45% by September, 75% by December, 100% by March.

sections.title: FIN-M10-L04: File your own income tax return, step by step
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Choose the right return form, walk through the online filing flow on the e-filing portal, and e-verify on time, knowing the due dates and what happens if you are late. **Time:** about 2 hours (20 minutes reading, 30 minutes resources, 70 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Which form?

- **ITR-1 (Sahaj):** for resident individuals with total income up to **₹50 lakh** from salary or pension, up to two house properties, other sources such as interest, agricultural income up to ₹5,000, and long-term gains on listed equity up to ₹1.25 lakh. Not for business or professional income, short-term capital gains, or larger capital gains ([ITR-1 user manual](https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/newdownloads/itr/itr-UM)).
- **Other forms** cover capital gains beyond those limits, business and professional income (including presumptive taxation), and other cases. The portal asks questions and suggests the right form.

Form names and numbers may change for returns under the new Act; follow what the portal shows for your tax year.

### Before you start

- **PAN active and linked to Aadhaar**; a **bank account pre-validated** on the portal for refunds.
- **AIS checked** (FIN-M10-L01), all documents collected (your checklist).
- Your Tax tab result, so you know roughly what the answer should be.

### The online flow (from the ITR-1 user manual)

1. Log in to the e-filing portal: **e-File → Income Tax Returns → File Income Tax Return**.
2. Choose the **assessment/tax year** and **Online** mode, then your filing status (individual).
3. Choose the form (the portal can help you pick).
4. **Regime:** the new regime is the default; to use the old one, you opt out at this step (with business income, the opt-out has its own form and deadline).
5. **Review the pre-filled data**: your details, income, TDS and bank accounts come from your records and AIS. Correct and add what is missing (for example, savings interest).
6. Enter deductions (old regime only) and check the tax computation.
7. **Pay any tax due** through **e-Pay Tax**, then enter the challan details.
8. **Preview, validate and submit.**
9. **e-Verify within 30 days**: by Aadhaar OTP, net banking, a bank or demat account electronic verification code, or a digital signature. If you don't verify (or send the signed ITR-V by post to CPC Bengaluru) within 30 days, the return is treated as **invalid**.

([ITR-1 user manual](https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/newdownloads/itr/itr-UM), check current rules.)

### Due dates and lateness

- **31 July:** individuals without business income and without audit.
- **31 August:** individuals with business or professional income that doesn't need an audit (from Finance Act 2026; AY 2026-27 returns of this type were due 31 August 2026) ([ETV Bharat](https://www.etvbharat.com/en/business/over-7-crore-itrs-filed-for-ay27-deadline-ends-tonight-enn26083106916)).
- **31 October:** cases needing an audit.
- **Late:** a **belated return** can still be filed within 9 months after the end of the tax year, with a late fee of **₹1,000 if total income is up to ₹5 lakh, and ₹5,000 otherwise**; a **revised return** to correct mistakes can be filed within 12 months after the end of the tax year ([section 263](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-263-72), [Finance Bill 2026 notes](https://incometaxindia.gov.in/Budgets%20and%20Bills/2026/Notes-on-clauses-2026.pdf), check current rules).

### After filing

Track the status on the portal: processed, refund issued, or a notice. Read every notice on the portal itself. **Never click links in SMS or emails about "tax refunds"**: they are a common phishing trick (Module 15).

## Local example

**Anu** filed her first return in July for the previous year's income of about ₹1,90,000 (tuition fees and interest), to claim back ₹2,840 of TDS.

Her tuition income counted as income from a profession, so ITR-1 wasn't right for her; the portal pointed her to the form for presumptive income (FIN-M10-L05). She followed the same flow: the pre-filled data showed the coaching centre's TDS and her bank interest; she added her home tuition receipts from her log; the tax computed was ₹0; the refund was ₹2,840.

She e-verified with an Aadhaar OTP the same evening. The refund arrived in her pre-validated bank account five weeks later. Total time: about two hours, most of it spent collecting her receipts. "Next year: 40 minutes," she wrote, "because my log already has everything."

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Income Tax e-filing: ITR-1 (Sahaj) user manual](https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/newdownloads/itr/itr-UM) | The ITR-1 user manual: eligibility, prerequisites, the step-by-step flow and e-verification | 30 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Income-tax Act, 2025, section 263: return of income and due dates](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-263-72) | Section 263: due dates, belated and revised returns | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Finance Bill 2026: notes on clauses (PDF): due dates, late fee, TDS](https://incometaxindia.gov.in/Budgets%20and%20Bills/2026/Notes-on-clauses-2026.pdf) | Finance Bill 2026 notes on clauses: the 31 August date, revised returns and the late fee (search for "263" and "428") | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Log in to the e-filing portal. Check your profile: PAN–Aadhaar link, contact details and a pre-validated bank account (add one if missing).
2. Find which form fits you this year, using the manual and the portal's questions.
3. If you have income to report for a year whose return is due or still allowed, file it, following the flow, and e-verify the same day.
4. If you have nothing to file now, do a **dry run**: open the filing flow for the latest year, go through the screens up to the preview without submitting, and note each step.
5. Put the due date for next year's return in your calendar, with a reminder two weeks earlier to check AIS.

**Proof to record:** Your filing acknowledgement and e-verification confirmation (PAN covered), or your dry-run notes with screenshots of the steps, saved in 10 Tax.

## Template: ITR filing checklist

```
BEFORE
[ ] PAN active, linked to Aadhaar
[ ] Bank account pre-validated for refunds
[ ] AIS/TIS checked; errors reported
[ ] Documents ready (salary TDS certificate, interest certificates, CAS, receipts)
[ ] Regime decided (Tax tab)
DURING
[ ] Correct form and tax year
[ ] Pre-filled data checked line by line; missing income added (savings interest!)
[ ] Tax computed matches my Tax tab roughly
[ ] Tax due paid through e-Pay Tax; challan entered
AFTER
[ ] Submitted on ____ (acknowledgement number saved)
[ ] e-Verified on ____ (within 30 days)
[ ] Status checked after 2-4 weeks; refund received on ____
```

## Common mistakes

- **Forgetting savings account interest.** It is taxable income and appears in AIS; add it.
- **Not e-verifying.** An unverified return becomes invalid after 30 days. Verify the same day.
- **Filing at the last minute.** Portal delays and missing documents cause late fees. File in early July.
- **Clicking "refund" links in messages.** Check refunds only on the portal itself.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Within how many days must you verify your return after filing?
    - A) 120 days
    - B) There is no limit
    - C) 7 days
    - D) 30 days
2. Who can use ITR-1 (Sahaj), per the user manual?
    - A) NRIs only
    - B) Resident individuals with income up to ₹50 lakh from salary, up to two house properties and other sources
    - C) Companies
    - D) Anyone with business income
3. What is the late fee for a belated return if total income is ₹4 lakh, as of November 2026?
    - A) ₹1,000
    - B) Nil
    - C) ₹10,000
    - D) ₹5,000
4. Due date for an individual with freelance income who doesn't need an audit, from Finance Act 2026?
    - A) 31 March
    - B) 31 December
    - C) 31 August
    - D) 31 July

## Progress checklist

1. **D.** Otherwise the return is treated as invalid.
2. **B.** Business income, short-term gains and larger capital gains need other forms.
3. **A.** ₹1,000 if total income is up to ₹5 lakh; ₹5,000 otherwise.
4. **C.** The new date for non-audit business and professional cases is 31 August.
