sections.title: FIN-M13-L01: Nominations and joint accounts
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Check and update nominees on every account, deposit, policy and investment under the 2025–2026 rules, and understand what a nominee and a joint holder can and can't do. **Time:** about 1 hour 30 minutes (20 minutes reading, 20 minutes resources, 50 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

Every year, money sits unclaimed in Indian banks, insurance companies and mutual funds because the owner died and the family didn't know about the account, or couldn't prove their right to it. A few minutes on nominations saves your family months of paperwork and stress.

### What a nomination does

A **nominee** is the person the bank, insurer or fund house pays when you die. With a nominee on record, your family can receive the money with simple documents, without court papers. Who finally **owns** the money can still depend on your will or on succession law; a will (FIN-M13-L02) makes your wishes clear to everyone. So do both: nominate, and write a will when you have dependants or significant assets.

### Bank accounts, deposits and lockers: up to four nominees

Under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, from **1 November 2025** you can nominate **up to four people** ([PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2181734), [IIBF](https://iibf.org.in/documents/Brochure/2025/Nomination_Under_Banking_Laws_AmendmentAct_2025.pdf), check current rules):

- **Deposit accounts:** either **simultaneous** nomination (each nominee gets a share you specify, adding up to 100%) or **successive** nomination (the next nominee becomes entitled only if the one above has died).
- **Lockers and articles in safe custody:** **successive** nomination only.
- The detailed rules and forms come under the Banking Companies (Nomination) Rules, 2025; ask your bank for the current form.

### Demat accounts and mutual funds: up to three nominees

SEBI's circular of **29 May 2026**, effective **1 September 2026**, allows **up to three nominees** for demat accounts and mutual fund folios. For **single-holder** accounts and folios opened from that date, you must either **nominate or submit an opt-out declaration**; for joint holdings, nomination is optional and changes need all holders' consent. It replaced the January 2025 circular, which had allowed up to ten ([SEBI circular, via NSDL](https://nsdl.com/nsdl/2026-08/32%20SEBI%20Circular%20dated%2029%20May%202026.pdf), check current rules). Your consolidated account statement shows each folio's nomination status ([AMFI CAS](https://www.amfiindia.com/investor-corner/investor-center/cas.html)).

### Insurance, EPF, PPF, NPS and government schemes

Each policy and account has its own nomination: life and accident policies, EPF (on the EPFO member services), PPF (at the post office or bank), NPS, PMJJBY and PMSBY, and for Kerala government employees, GPF and other schemes (Module 14). Check each one; a nomination made at 22 may name someone you wouldn't choose at 32.

### Joint accounts

A joint account is owned by two or more people. Its **operating instruction**, chosen when it was opened (for example "either or survivor"), decides who can use it, including after one holder dies. Ask your bank which instruction your joint accounts have. Joint accounts are useful for couples and for elderly parents who need help with banking, but every holder can usually withdraw money, so open them only with people you trust.

### Lost and unclaimed money

Deposits that stay unclaimed for many years are moved by banks to RBI's Depositor Education and Awareness (DEA) Fund, but they can still be claimed. RBI's **UDGAM** portal lets registered users search unclaimed deposits across many banks (30 banks covering about 90% of the fund's value, as of March 2024) by name, bank and an identifier such as PAN or date of birth; the claim itself is made at the bank ([RBI UDGAM FAQs](https://rbi.org.in/scripts/FS_FAQs.aspx?Id=166)). Use it for yourself and for relatives who have died.

## Local example

**Fathima** made a list of everything in her name and checked nominees one by one. She found:

| Account | Nominee before | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Savings account (Bank A) | None | Added her mother (simultaneous, 100%) |
| Savings account (Bank B) | Her late grandfather | Changed to her mother and brother, 50% each |
| PPF | Her father (opened when she was 20) | Kept, after checking he is still the right choice |
| Two-wheeler insurance | Not applicable (property) | — |
| PMSBY (₹20 accident cover) | None recorded | Added her mother at the branch |
| NPS (new) | Her mother | Already done at opening |

The grandfather was the shock: had something happened to her, Bank B would have been paying a dead person's estate. She also searched UDGAM for her grandfather, with her uncle's help, and found an old savings account with ₹38,000 at a bank in Thalassery, which the family then claimed at the branch with the documents the bank asked for.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [PIB: up to four nominees for bank accounts from 1 November 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2181734) | The four-nominee rules for bank deposits and lockers, from 1 November 2025 | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [IIBF: nomination under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 (PDF)](https://iibf.org.in/documents/Brochure/2025/Nomination_Under_Banking_Laws_AmendmentAct_2025.pdf) | Simultaneous and successive nomination explained | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [SEBI circular on nominations for demat and mutual funds, 29 May 2026 (PDF, via NSDL)](https://nsdl.com/nsdl/2026-08/32%20SEBI%20Circular%20dated%2029%20May%202026.pdf) | SEBI's May 2026 circular on demat and mutual fund nominations: read the summary points | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [RBI: UDGAM FAQs (find unclaimed deposits)](https://rbi.org.in/scripts/FS_FAQs.aspx?Id=166) | How to search for unclaimed deposits on UDGAM | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Make a **Documents** tab and start with the nomination audit template: every account, deposit, locker, policy, investment and retirement account in your name.
2. For each, check the current nominee: in the bank app, the CAS, policy documents, EPFO member services, or by asking the branch.
3. Update at least the most important missing or outdated nominee this week; note the acknowledgement.
4. Ask your bank about the operating instruction on any joint account and write it down.
5. Search UDGAM for yourself, and (with family) for a relative who has died, if relevant.

**Proof to record:** Your nomination audit with every account checked and proof of at least one nominee update (acknowledgement or screenshot, numbers covered), saved in 13 Estate.

## Template: nomination audit (Documents tab)

```csv
Account or policy,Institution,Last 4 digits,Nominee(s),Shares % (simultaneous) or order (successive),Last checked,Needs change?,Done on
Savings account,,,,,,,
Fixed/recurring deposits,,,,,,,
Locker,,,,(successive only),,,
Demat account,,,,(up to 3),,,
Mutual fund folios (from CAS),,,,(up to 3),,,
Life/term insurance,,,,,,,
Health/accident insurance,,,,,,,
EPF / PPF / NPS,,,,,,,
PMJJBY / PMSBY / APY,,,,,,,
GPF / govt schemes (if employee),,,,,,,
```

## Common mistakes

- **Thinking "my family will manage".** Without nominees, claims can need legal heir certificates and months of visits.
- **Never updating nominations.** Marriage, a death or a child should trigger a check of every nomination.
- **Assuming a nominee always owns the money.** The nominee receives it; ownership can depend on your will or succession law. Write a will too.
- **Opening joint accounts casually.** Every holder can usually withdraw. Choose joint holders you trust completely.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. From 1 November 2025, how many nominees can you name for a bank deposit account?
    - A) Only one
    - B) Up to four
    - C) None
    - D) Up to ten
2. For a bank locker, which type of nomination is allowed?
    - A) Successive only
    - B) None
    - C) Simultaneous only
    - D) Both
3. Under SEBI's circular effective 1 September 2026, how many nominees can a demat account have?
    - A) Up to ten
    - B) Unlimited
    - C) Up to three
    - D) Only one
4. What can UDGAM do?
    - A) Pay the claim directly
    - B) Help you search unclaimed deposits across many banks
    - C) Make your will
    - D) Change your nominee

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The four-nominee rules (PIB, IIBF), SEBI's May 2026 nomination circular and the UDGAM FAQs
- **Action:** Audit nominees on every account and policy, update at least one, and search UDGAM. It is done when your proof is saved: your nomination audit with every account checked and proof of at least one nominee update (acknowledgement or screenshot, numbers covered), saved in 13 Estate.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** The Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 allows up to four, simultaneously or successively.
2. **A.** Lockers and safe custody articles allow only successive nomination.
3. **C.** The May 2026 circular replaced the earlier ten-nominee rule (check current rules).
4. **B.** It shows where unclaimed deposits are; you claim at the bank.

sections.title: FIN-M13-L02: Wills and your family money file
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Decide whether you need a will now, know the basic rules for a valid will in India, and build a family money file and document register so your family can find everything. **Time:** about 1 hour 30 minutes (25 minutes reading, 20 minutes resources, 45 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Why a will

A **will** says who gets your property after you die and who should handle it (the executor). Without one, your property passes under the succession law that applies to you, which may not match your wishes, and families often need court documents to prove who the heirs are. A will is not only for the rich: if you have a spouse, children, a house, a plot or savings, it protects them.

### Basics for a valid will in India

From a legal guide on making and registering a will ([iPleaders](https://blog.ipleaders.in/register-will-india/)):

- Any **adult of sound mind** can make a will.
- An ordinary written will must be **signed by you and attested by two witnesses**.
- **Registration is not compulsory** (Registration Act, 1908, section 18), but registering it makes it stronger if anyone disputes it.
- You can change or revoke a will at any time; **a later will replaces an earlier one**. Under the Indian Succession Act, a **marriage revokes an earlier will**, so make a new one after marrying.
- The Indian Succession Act's will rules don't apply to Muslims, who are generally governed by Muslim personal law; Muslims should get advice on what share can be willed.
- Probate (court confirmation of a will) is needed in some cases; a lawyer can tell you whether it applies to you.

### What a simple will includes

Your full name and details; a statement that you are making it freely and revoke earlier wills; a list of your main assets (described, not necessarily with full account numbers); who receives what, with backup beneficiaries; an **executor**; a **guardian** for minor children; the date and place; your signature and two witnesses' signatures (it is safer to choose witnesses who receive nothing under the will). For property, a business, family disputes or Gulf/NRI assets, **pay a lawyer**: a mistake in a will can't be fixed after you are gone.

### Your family money file

A will is useless if no one can find the accounts. A **family money file** is a simple document (paper, and a protected digital copy) that tells a trusted person:

- Every bank account, deposit, locker, investment, policy and loan: institution, branch, type, last four digits, nominee
- Where original documents are: property deeds, policy bonds, PAN, Aadhaar, certificates
- Digital accounts that matter (email, the Money Folder) and how to get help to access them, **without writing passwords** in the file (keep those separately, sealed, or in a password manager whose master password is shared safely)
- Who to call: a trusted relative, the employer, an insurance agent, a lawyer or tax helper
- Your wishes on important matters

### DigiLocker

**DigiLocker** (by MeitY under Digital India) stores digital copies of documents such as Aadhaar, PAN, voter ID, driving licence, vehicle registration and marksheets, and lets you share them ([DigiLocker](https://www.digilocker.gov.in/)). Use it for government-issued documents; keep policy bonds and property papers safe too.

### Review

Check the file and nominations once a year (your yearly review), and update the will after marriage, children, a death in the family, or a big asset change.

## Local example

**Joseph and Mary** had no will: "Our son is the only child; it's obvious." Anu asked them what would happen to the house if their son were abroad and Mary were unwell, or if a relative challenged it. They agreed to see a lawyer in Vatakara, who drafted simple wills for both (each leaving everything to the other, then to their son), with two neighbours as witnesses, and registered them at the sub-registrar office for a modest fee.

Their son built the family money file over a weekend: 3 bank accounts, 2 FDs, the post office MIS, the house deed (in the steel almirah), the pension papers, the KASP card and the locker key's location. The file is in a sealed envelope at home, with a copy in the son's DigiLocker-linked Drive folder (without passwords). Mary said the best part was "knowing he won't have to search in a hurry".

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [iPleaders: how to make and register a will in India](https://blog.ipleaders.in/register-will-india/) | How to make and register a will in India: validity, witnesses, registration, revoking | 20 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [DigiLocker](https://www.digilocker.gov.in/) | What DigiLocker stores and how to fetch your documents | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [RBI: UDGAM FAQs (find unclaimed deposits)](https://rbi.org.in/scripts/FS_FAQs.aspx?Id=166) | Revise: finding unclaimed deposits of a family member | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Add a **document register** to your Documents tab: every important document, where the original is, and whether a digital copy is in DigiLocker or your Money Folder.
2. Sign in to DigiLocker and fetch at least your Aadhaar, PAN and one more issued document.
3. Write your family money file using the template, without passwords, and decide where it is kept and who knows.
4. Decide whether you need a will now (dependants, a house or land, significant savings). If yes, draft the outline and plan when you will see a lawyer or write and sign it with two witnesses. If not yet, write the life event that will trigger it.
5. Tell your trusted person where the file is.

**Proof to record:** A screenshot of your document register, the family money file (contents covered as needed) and your will decision, saved in 13 Estate.

## Template: document register

```csv
Document,Original kept at,Digital copy (DigiLocker / Money Folder / none),Valid until,Who knows where it is
PAN,,,,
Aadhaar,,,,
Birth certificate,,,,
Educational certificates,,,,
Property deed and tax receipts,,,,
Insurance policies,,,,
Vehicle RC and insurance,,,,
Bank passbooks and FD receipts,,,,
Pension / service records (if employee),,,,
Will (if made),,,,
```

## Template: family money file (no passwords)

```
IF SOMETHING HAPPENS TO ME (updated on ____)
1. Accounts and deposits: institution, branch, type, last 4 digits, nominee (see Documents tab)
2. Insurance policies: insurer, type, cover, where the policy is, claim helpline
3. Investments and retirement accounts: EPF/PPF/NPS/funds/demat, where statements are
4. Loans I owe and money owed to me
5. Where originals are kept: ____
6. Will: made? yes/no; kept at ____; executor ____
7. Digital: email and Money Folder; how to get help to access them: ____ (no passwords here)
8. People to contact: relative ____ employer ____ lawyer/tax helper ____
9. My wishes: ____
```

## Template: simple will outline (take to a lawyer or adapt carefully)

```
I, ____ (name, parent's name, age, address), being of sound mind, make this will freely and revoke all earlier wills.
My assets include: ____ (describe)
I leave ____ to ____; if they die before me, to ____.
I appoint ____ as executor. For my minor children, I appoint ____ as guardian.
Signed on ____ at ____.   Signature: ____
Witness 1 (name, address, signature): ____   Witness 2: ____
```

## Common mistakes

- **Thinking wills are only for the rich or old.** A spouse, a child or a plot is reason enough.
- **Writing passwords in the money file.** Keep them separately and securely; the file says how to get help, not the secrets.
- **Not updating after marriage.** Under the Indian Succession Act, marriage revokes an earlier will.
- **DIY wills for complex situations.** Property disputes, businesses and NRI assets need a lawyer.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Is registering a will compulsory in India?
    - A) No, but it strengthens the will in a dispute
    - B) Yes, always
    - C) Only in Kerala
    - D) Only for women
2. How many witnesses must attest an ordinary written will?
    - A) One
    - B) Two
    - C) None
    - D) Five
3. You made a will at 25 and married at 28. Under the Indian Succession Act, what happened to the will?
    - A) It became registered
    - B) The marriage revoked it; make a new one
    - C) Nothing
    - D) It doubled
4. What should a family money file never contain?
    - A) Where documents are kept
    - B) Passwords and OTPs
    - C) A list of accounts
    - D) Contact people

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The guide to making and registering a will, DigiLocker and UDGAM
- **Action:** Build a document register and family money file, fetch documents into DigiLocker and make a will decision. It is done when your proof is saved: a screenshot of your document register, the family money file (contents covered as needed) and your will decision, saved in 13 Estate.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** Section 18 of the Registration Act makes it optional.
2. **B.** An unprivileged will needs two witnesses.
3. **B.** Marriage revokes an earlier will under the Act.
4. **B.** Keep secrets separately; the file explains where things are.

Action: Build a document register and family money file, fetch documents into DigiLocker and make a will decision
tasks.detail: **Proof to record:** A screenshot of your document register, the family money file (contents covered as needed) and your will decision, saved in 13 Estate. Save it in your Money Folder and paste its link (or a short note of where it is) in this task's note. Never paste account numbers, passwords or OTPs anywhere.

sections.title: Module 14: Finance for a Kerala government employee
sections.summary: Prepare for the money side of a Kerala government job: read your pay slip, track DA and arrears, understand the pension situation honestly, use GPF and Medisep well, and follow a first-year plan.
sections.content:
## Overview

If your PSC preparation succeeds, your first salary will be the biggest change in your money life. A government job brings stable income, DA increases, health cover through Medisep and retirement contributions, and also new traps: budgeting on gross pay, spending arrears, office insurance-investment plans and easy salary-recovery loans.

As of November 2026, Kerala's pension arrangements were in flux: a contributory scheme since 2013, an Assured Pension Scheme announced in March 2026, and a new government in August 2026 saying it would reform the contributory scheme instead. This module shows you how to plan sensibly under that uncertainty. If you aren't an employee yet, do it as a what-if; you'll thank yourself in your first month.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Read every line of a Kerala government pay slip and budget on take-home pay
- Track DA changes and plan arrears with the half-raise rule
- Explain the 2026 pension situation and plan a personal corpus alongside it
- Use GPF and Medisep well, with nominations and dependants in order
- Follow a first-year money plan for a new government job

## Time

About 5 hours in total: 4 hours of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: week 27.

## Lessons

1. FIN-M14-L01: Your pay slip decoded: basic pay, DA, deductions and SPARK (about 2 hours)
2. FIN-M14-L02: Pension, GPF, Medisep and your first-year money plan (about 2 hours)

## Module project: My government-job money plan (real or what-if)

1. Complete the Pay Slip tab for your job or a what-if post.
2. Write your pension note and your personal retirement saving plan.
3. Complete the first-year money plan with dates.
4. Update your Budget, Insurance and Retirement tabs with the pay slip numbers.
5. Add the government-employee items to your yearly review checklist.

**Proof to record:** The Pay Slip tab, pension note and first-year plan, saved in 14 Govt job.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pay slip | Not read | Earnings understood | Every line classified and budget based on take-home |
| DA and arrears | No plan | Aware of DA | Rule for DA rises and arrears written |
| Pension | Assumes it is settled | Knows the scheme name | Understands the 2026 uncertainty and plans a personal corpus |
| GPF and Medisep | Unknown | Partly checked | Rules known, nominations and dependants checked |
| First-year plan | None | A list | Dated plan with rules for loans and insurance offers |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Decode one pay slip (FIN-M14-L01).
- Write your pension note and start a small personal retirement saving (FIN-M14-L02).
- Check Medisep dependants and nominations.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Kerala DA and DR from the October 2026 order | 37% (from 35%), arrears from 1 January 2026. |
| Contributory pension scheme in Kerala | For employees joining from 1 April 2013. |
| Government contribution to the contributory scheme, 2026 | 10% (employees have demanded 14%). |
| Assured Pension Scheme status, August 2026 | Announced in March 2026, not implemented; new government plans to reform the contributory scheme. |
| GPF minimum subscription | 6% of basic pay. |
| GPF nominations and closure | Through SPARK; family members only as nominees. |
| Medisep phase 2 | ₹5 lakh a year, ₹687 a month, no age limit, from 1 February 2026. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Thinking a government job means no planning.** Stable income makes planning easier, not unnecessary.
- **Letting lifestyle rise with every DA increase.** Use the half-raise rule every time.
- **Ignoring pension news.** Check every year; decisions about switching schemes deserve careful reading.

sections.title: FIN-M14-L01: Your pay slip decoded: basic pay, DA, deductions and SPARK
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Read a Kerala government pay slip line by line, track DA changes and arrears, and turn the take-home figure into your budget. **Time:** about 2 hours (25 minutes reading, 25 minutes resources, 70 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

This module is for the day your PSC result turns into an appointment order. If you aren't a government employee yet, do it as a "what-if" with a realistic entry post; it will make your first month in the job much easier. If a relative is a government employee, use their pay slip with permission.

### Earnings

- **Basic pay:** fixed by your post's pay scale and your stage in it; it rises with yearly increments and with pay revisions decided by government order.
- **Dearness allowance (DA):** a percentage of basic pay that compensates for price rises, revised by government order. Kerala raised **DA and dearness relief (for pensioners) from 35% to 37%** by an order dated 17 October 2026 (G.O.(P) No.108/2026/Fin, listed on the [Finance Department website](https://finance.kerala.gov.in/), where DA, pay and other orders are published); the new DA came with the October salary paid in November 2026, and **arrears from 1 January 2026** are to follow by a separate order ([Onmanorama, October 2026](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2026/10/17/kerala-hikes-da-dr-by-2-revised-rates-effective-with-november-payments.html), check current rules).
- **House rent allowance (HRA)** and other allowances, depending on your post and place of work.

### Deductions

- **Pension contribution:** employees who joined from **1 April 2013** are in the **contributory pension scheme** (NPS) ([Moneylife](https://moneylife.in/article/introduction-of-contributory-pension-scheme-in-kerala/30913.html)); a share of basic pay plus DA is deducted, and the government also contributes (FIN-M14-L02). Employees in the older statutory pension contribute to the **General Provident Fund (GPF)** instead.
- **Medisep:** the state's health insurance scheme for employees and pensioners; the premium from February 2026 is **₹687 a month** (FIN-M14-L02).
- **Insurance schemes for employees,** such as the Group Personal Accident Insurance Scheme (GPAIS), whose policy year starts every January ([CUSAT circular](https://finance.cusat.ac.in/uploads/CIRC_279_CUSAT_NPS.N3_GPAIS_2024-2025.pdf)); check the amounts on your pay slip.
- **Profession tax:** collected half-yearly through your employer for the local body; the maximum any state can levy is ₹2,500 a year ([Kerala LSGD FAQs](https://professiontax.lsgkerala.gov.in/faq.php)).
- **Income tax (TDS):** your drawing and disbursing officer (DDO) deducts it based on the regime you choose (Module 10).
- **Recoveries:** advances, loans from the government or from co-operative societies deducted from salary.

### A worked pay slip (made-up numbers except the DA rate and Medisep)

| Line | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Basic pay (made-up) | ₹27,000 |
| DA at 37% of basic | ₹9,990 |
| HRA (made-up) | ₹1,500 |
| **Gross** | **₹38,490** |
| Pension contribution, 10% of basic + DA (check your slip) | −₹3,699 |
| Medisep premium | −₹687 |
| Other insurance and small deductions (made-up) | −₹500 |
| **Take-home** (before any income tax, profession tax months or recoveries) | **₹33,604** |

### SPARK

**SPARK** is the Kerala government's payroll and service records system. Your pay slips, service details and several employee services, such as GPF nominations and closures, go through it ([AG Kerala](https://cag.gov.in/ae/kerala/en/page-ae-kerala-about-gpf)). Learn to read your own records there early, and keep personal details (bank account, nominees, address) correct.

### Budget on take-home, plan for arrears

Your budget starts from **take-home pay**, not gross. DA increases and arrears are **raises**: use the half-raise rule from Module 1 (at least half goes to your goals or emergency fund), and decide what the arrears will do **before** they arrive.

## Local example

**Rahul** received his first full month's pay as an LD clerk and, like many new employees, felt confused by the slip. He copied every line into the pay slip tracker from this lesson. Three things became clear:

1. His take-home was about 20% below gross. He had budgeted on gross for a month before he noticed.
2. His pension deduction was going into the contributory pension scheme, because he joined after April 2013. He hadn't known that his pension would depend on those contributions and their returns (FIN-M14-L02).
3. Profession tax appeared only in some months; he added it to his sinking funds so those months didn't surprise him.

When the DA increase to 37% was announced in October 2026, his tracker showed the monthly rise (2% of his basic). He sent half of it to his emergency fund by standing instruction and decided that the DA arrears from January would go entirely to clearing his phone EMI and then his goals.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Onmanorama: Kerala raises DA and DR to 37% (October 2026)](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2026/10/17/kerala-hikes-da-dr-by-2-revised-rates-effective-with-november-payments.html) | The October 2026 DA and DR increase: rates and when they are paid | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Kerala Finance Department: government orders and circulars (DA, pay, Medisep link)](https://finance.kerala.gov.in/) | The Finance Department website: find the DA order and the list of recent government orders | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Moneylife: Kerala introduces the contributory pension scheme for employees joining from 1 April 2013](https://moneylife.in/article/introduction-of-contributory-pension-scheme-in-kerala/30913.html) | Why employees who joined from April 2013 are in the contributory pension scheme | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Accountant General (A&E) Kerala: about GPF](https://cag.gov.in/ae/kerala/en/page-ae-kerala-about-gpf) | The AG Kerala GPF page, including what goes through SPARK | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Kerala LSGD: profession tax FAQs](https://professiontax.lsgkerala.gov.in/faq.php) | Profession tax basics | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Get a pay slip: yours, a relative's (with permission and numbers covered), or build a what-if slip for the post you are preparing for, using a realistic basic pay from its notification.
2. Make a **Pay Slip** tab with the template and enter every line.
3. Check the DA line against the current DA rate; note any arrears due.
4. Mark each deduction: savings (pension, GPF), insurance (Medisep, GPAIS), tax, or a loan recovery.
5. Update your Budget tab so it starts from take-home pay, and write your plan for the next DA increase and any arrears.

**Proof to record:** Your Pay Slip tab with every line classified, the DA check and your plan for DA increases and arrears, saved in 14 Govt job.

## Template: Pay Slip tab

```
B2: basic pay (₹)            B3: DA rate (e.g. 0.37)          B4: HRA (₹)        B5: other allowances (₹)
B6: DA (₹)                   =B2*B3
B7: gross (₹)                =B2+B6+B4+B5
B9: pension contribution     =ROUND((B2+B6)*0.10,0)     (or the GPF subscription, at least 6% of basic, if in GPF)
B10: Medisep (₹)             687
B11: GPAIS and other insurance (₹)
B12: profession tax this month (₹)     B13: income tax (TDS) this month (₹)     B14: recoveries (₹)
B15: total deductions        =SUM(B9:B14)
B16: take-home               =B7-B15
DA change check: new DA rate in B18 → monthly rise =B2*(B18-B3)
Arrears estimate: months due × monthly rise =B19*B2*(B18-B3)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Budgeting on gross pay.** Your budget starts from take-home.
- **Treating arrears as a bonus to spend.** Decide in advance; arrears are a perfect emergency fund or debt payoff boost.
- **Ignoring pay slip errors.** Check every line every month; raise errors with your office early.
- **Taking salary-recovery loans for wants.** Easy deductions from salary still cost interest and reduce take-home for years.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What was Kerala's DA rate after the October 2026 order?
    - A) 12%
    - B) 50%
    - C) 37%
    - D) 35%
2. Basic pay ₹30,000 and DA rises by 2 percentage points. How much more DA per month?
    - A) ₹60
    - B) ₹2,000
    - C) ₹6,000
    - D) ₹600
3. Kerala employees who joined service from 1 April 2013 are in which pension arrangement?
    - A) No pension
    - B) The Atal Pension Yojana
    - C) The old statutory pension with GPF only
    - D) The contributory pension scheme
4. Your budget should start from…
    - A) Gross pay
    - B) Take-home pay
    - C) Last year's DA
    - D) Basic pay

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The DA order report, the contributory pension background, the AG Kerala GPF page and profession tax basics
- **Action:** Decode a real or what-if pay slip in a Pay Slip tab and plan for DA increases and arrears. It is done when your proof is saved: your Pay Slip tab with every line classified, the DA check and your plan for DA increases and arrears, saved in 14 Govt job.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** It rose from 35% to 37%, with arrears from 1 January 2026 (check current rules).
2. **D.** 2% of ₹30,000 = ₹600.
3. **D.** Kerala introduced the contributory pension scheme for employees joining from that date.
4. **B.** Deductions never reach your account; plan with what does.

sections.title: FIN-M14-L02: Pension, GPF, Medisep and your first-year money plan
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Understand where Kerala's pension arrangements stood in 2026, how GPF and Medisep work, and follow a first-year money plan for a new government job. **Time:** about 2 hours (25 minutes reading, 25 minutes resources, 70 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Pension: what is known, and what isn't, as of November 2026

- **Contributory pension (NPS) for those who joined from 1 April 2013:** the employee and the government contribute; the government's share is **10%**, and employee organisations have been demanding 14%, gratuity and a minimum pension ([Onmanorama, August 2026](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2026/08/17/kerala-govt-employees-left-waiting-pension-remains-stuck-between-promises.html)).
- **The Assured Pension Scheme (APS):** in March 2026, the then government gave in-principle sanction for an APS from 1 April 2026, with a pension of up to 50% of last basic pay (capped), dearness relief, and full pension after 30 years' qualifying service; new appointees were to choose between NPS and APS, and existing NPS members could switch ([Onmanorama, March 2026](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2026/03/01/assured-pension-scheme-kerala-government.html)).
- **After the change of government:** an August 2026 report says the new UDF government announced that the earlier plans were cancelled and that the contributory scheme would be **reformed** instead; as of then, neither the reform nor the APS had been implemented, and there was **no option to move to the Centre's Unified Pension Scheme** ([Onmanorama, August 2026](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2026/08/17/kerala-govt-employees-left-waiting-pension-remains-stuck-between-promises.html)).

**What this means for your plan:** the rules may change again. Plan your retirement (Module 12) assuming your pension comes from your contributory account and its returns, and build an additional personal corpus. If a better guaranteed pension arrives, your plan simply becomes safer. **Check current rules** before any decision such as switching schemes.

### GPF (for employees in pensionable service)

From the Accountant General (A&E) Kerala ([AG Kerala](https://cag.gov.in/ae/kerala/en/page-ae-kerala-about-gpf), check current rules):

- For permanent employees in pensionable service (and others as the rules allow). If you are in the contributory scheme, ask your office whether GPF applies to you.
- Subscription of **at least 6% of basic pay**, up to the full basic pay; you can reduce it once and increase it twice a year.
- Interest at the rate the Government of India sets for GPF and Kerala adopts (**7.1%** in the recent periods shown on the page), credited at the end of the year. Interest on subscriptions above **₹5 lakh a year** is taxable.
- **Temporary advances** up to 75% of the balance; **non-refundable withdrawals** after 10 years' service or within 10 years of retirement.
- **Nominations and closure through SPARK** (family members only as nominees); the yearly account statement is on the AG's portal; report errors within 3 months. Help desk: 0471-2776650 / 0471-2330311.

### Medisep (phase 2 from 1 February 2026)

Kerala's medical insurance for state employees and pensioners: **₹5 lakh cover a year** (up from ₹3 lakh), premium **₹687 a month**, covering employees, pensioners, university and local body staff and dependants (about 32 lakh people), **with no age limit**; the insurer is Oriental Insurance, with 2,516 treatment packages, room rent up to ₹5,000 and cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals ([Onmanorama, January 2026](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2026/01/21/medisep-kerala-phase-2-rollout-february1.html), check current rules). Check that your dependants are enrolled, and use the claim kit habits from FIN-M07-L05. Consider whether your family needs a super top-up above ₹5 lakh, and cover for any family members who aren't dependants under the scheme.

### Your first-year money plan

1. **Before joining:** a starter emergency fund; clear expensive debts (Module 6).
2. **First month:** decode your pay slip; set nominees for pension, GPF (if any), Medisep and insurance schemes through your office and SPARK; collect your Medisep card.
3. **Budget on take-home** with a half-raise rule for increments, DA and pay revisions (Module 1).
4. **Insurance:** Medisep is your health base. Add term cover if anyone depends on you (FIN-M07-L02). Say no to bundled policies sold at the office until you have calculated their return (FIN-M07-L01).
5. **Retirement:** start your own corpus alongside the pension contribution (Module 12).
6. **Tax:** choose your regime with your DDO using your calculator (FIN-M10-L02).
7. **Loans:** be careful with easy salary-recovery loans and co-operative loans for wants; they reduce take-home for years.
8. **Scams:** be wary of messages about "arrears", "pay fixation" or "pension portals" that ask for OTPs or payments (Module 15).

## Local example

**Rahul's** first-year plan, written in his second month:

| When | Action | Done? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Month 1 | Pay slip decoded; nominees set through the office for pension, Medisep and GPAIS | Yes |
| Month 2 | Budget on take-home; emergency fund transfer ₹4,000 a month | Yes |
| Month 3 | Term cover compared (FIN-M07-L02); the office "investment-insurance plan" declined after calculating its return | Yes |
| Month 4 | Own retirement SIP started at ₹1,500 a month with 10% yearly step-up | Planned |
| Every DA change | Half the rise to goals by standing instruction | Rule written |
| Arrears | Phone EMI cleared, then emergency fund | Rule written |
| Every year | Check the pension scheme news and Medisep renewal | In review checklist |

His colleague asked why he was saving separately for retirement "when the government gives a pension". Rahul showed her the two Onmanorama reports from March and August 2026: "Nobody knows yet what the final rules will be. My own corpus is the part I control."

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Onmanorama: Kerala employees still waiting on pension reform (August 2026)](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2026/08/17/kerala-govt-employees-left-waiting-pension-remains-stuck-between-promises.html) | The pension situation for Kerala employees as of August 2026 | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Onmanorama: Assured Pension Scheme sanctioned in principle (March 2026)](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2026/03/01/assured-pension-scheme-kerala-government.html) | The Assured Pension Scheme announced in March 2026 | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Accountant General (A&E) Kerala: about GPF](https://cag.gov.in/ae/kerala/en/page-ae-kerala-about-gpf) | GPF rules: subscription, interest, advances, withdrawals, nominations | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Onmanorama: Medisep phase 2 from 1 February 2026](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2026/01/21/medisep-kerala-phase-2-rollout-february1.html) | Medisep phase 2: cover, premium, who is covered | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Write which pension arrangement applies to you (or to the post you are preparing for), and what is still uncertain.
2. If you have or expect GPF, write your subscription plan (at least 6% of basic) and the advance/withdrawal rules you must remember.
3. Check Medisep: are all your dependants enrolled? Is a top-up needed for your family? Add it to your Insurance tab.
4. Fill in the first-year money plan template with dates, for your real job or a what-if.
5. Add "pension scheme news, Medisep renewal and GPF statement" to your yearly review.

**Proof to record:** Your pension note, GPF plan (if relevant), Medisep check and the first-year money plan, saved in 14 Govt job.

## Template: first-year money plan for a new government job

```
Before joining: starter emergency fund ₹____  | expensive debts cleared? ____
Month 1: pay slip decoded [ ]  nominees set (pension, GPF, Medisep, GPAIS) [ ]  Medisep card [ ]
Month 2: budget on take-home ₹____  | emergency fund transfer ₹____ on ____ (date)
Month 3: insurance: term cover needed? ____  | bundled office policies: return calculated ____
Month 4: own retirement saving ₹____ a month, step-up ___% a year, account ____
Tax: regime chosen with DDO: ____ (calculator result attached)
Rules: DA rise → ___% to goals | arrears → ____ | salary loans only for ____
Yearly: pension news, Medisep renewal, GPF statement, nominations
```

## Common mistakes

- **Assuming the pension is settled.** As of 2026, Kerala's pension rules were still being debated. Build your own corpus too.
- **Forgetting dependants in Medisep.** Check enrolment early, before anyone needs treatment.
- **Saying yes to office insurance-investment plans.** Calculate the return first (FIN-M07-L01); most do both jobs badly.
- **Using GPF advances for wants.** GPF is retirement money; use advances only for real needs.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. As of the August 2026 report, what was the status of the Assured Pension Scheme announced in March 2026?
    - A) Replaced by the Centre's UPS
    - B) Not implemented; the new government said the contributory scheme would be reformed instead
    - C) Fully implemented for everyone
    - D) Never announced
2. What is the minimum GPF subscription, per AG Kerala?
    - A) ₹500 a year
    - B) 12% of gross pay
    - C) No minimum
    - D) 6% of basic pay
3. What does Medisep phase 2 cover from February 2026?
    - A) Only accidents
    - B) ₹1 lakh for employees only
    - C) ₹5 lakh a year for employees, pensioners and dependants, with no age limit
    - D) Only pensioners over 80
4. Why should a new Kerala government employee build a personal retirement corpus too?
    - A) Pension rules were uncertain in 2026, and a personal corpus is the part they control
    - B) Medisep requires it
    - C) It is compulsory
    - D) GPF is closed

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The August 2026 and March 2026 pension reports, the AG Kerala GPF page and the Medisep phase 2 report
- **Action:** Write your pension note, GPF plan and Medisep check, and fill in the first-year money plan. It is done when your proof is saved: your pension note, GPF plan (if relevant), Medisep check and the first-year money plan, saved in 14 Govt job.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** Neither the APS nor the reform had been implemented then (check current rules).
2. **D.** At least 6% of basic pay, up to the full basic pay.
3. **C.** Cover rose from ₹3 lakh to ₹5 lakh, with a premium of ₹687 a month.
4. **A.** Whatever the final scheme, an extra corpus makes the plan safer.

sections.title: Module 15: Scams and fraud protection
sections.summary: Recognise investment and payment scams before they reach your money, set up habits and settings that block them, and know exactly where to report if something goes wrong.
sections.content:
## Overview

Everything else in this course can be undone in one afternoon by a fraud: a "guaranteed" scheme, a fake trading app, a QR code "to receive a refund", or a video call from a fake police officer. Kerala has seen large investment frauds, and payment frauds reach every family with a phone.

This module teaches the patterns behind the tricks (urgency, fear, authority, greed and kindness), the official registers you can check yourself (SEBI, RBI Sachet), the I4C advisory on "digital arrest", and the reporting routes: 1930, the cyber crime portal, Chakshu, Sachet, SCORES and the ombudsmen. Your **scam-proof habits** and a family briefing become part of your final plan.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Recognise Ponzi schemes, pyramid MLMs, fake trading apps and unregistered tipsters
- Check any investment offer against official registers
- Recognise payment frauds, including "digital arrest", and set up protective settings
- Report each kind of fraud to the right place, fast, with evidence
- Brief your family and agree a family code

## Time

About 6 hours 30 minutes in total: 5 hours 30 minutes of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: weeks 28–29.

## Lessons

1. FIN-M15-L01: Investment scams: Ponzi schemes, MLM, fake apps and finfluencers (about 2 hours)
2. FIN-M15-L02: Payment frauds: UPI and OTP tricks, phishing and "digital arrest" (about 2 hours)
3. FIN-M15-L03: Report fast, recover what you can, and protect your family (about 1 hour 30 minutes)

## Module project: My scam-proof habits and family briefing

1. Complete the scam-proof habits checklist with every item ticked or a date to fix it.
2. Make sure your payment set-up limits damage: a low-balance UPI account and a daily limit.
3. Keep the incident log and reporting routes ready in your Scam Check tab.
4. Hold the family scam briefing and agree the family code.
5. Add "family scam briefing" to your yearly review.

**Proof to record:** Your completed checklist, the incident log template ready, the family code and briefing notes, saved in 15 Scams.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Investment scams | Can't spot them | Knows some signs | Applies the five questions and checks registers |
| Payment frauds | Unaware | Knows the common tricks | Settings and habits in place, including UPI limits |
| Digital arrest | Unaware | Has heard of it | Can explain it and has briefed a family member |
| Reporting | Doesn't know where | Knows 1930 | Knows every route and has the incident log ready |
| Family | Not discussed | One person told | Briefing held and a family code agreed |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Save 1930 and the fraud response card (FIN-M15-L03).
- Set a daily UPI limit and keep savings in a non-UPI account (FIN-M15-L02).
- Teach one older family member about "digital arrest".

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Ponzi pattern | High "guaranteed" returns paid from new investors' money, plus rewards for recruiting. |
| Pyramid vs real direct selling | Pyramid: income from recruiting. Real: income from selling products to customers. |
| Fake trading app sign | Big profits you can't withdraw without paying a "fee" or "tax". |
| Digital arrest | Not real: CBI, police, customs, ED and judges don't arrest anyone on video calls. |
| Lost money? | Call 1930, block with the bank, report at cybercrime.gov.in. |
| Suspicious call or SMS, no loss? | Report it on Chakshu (Sanchar Saathi). |
| Illegal deposit scheme? | Complain on RBI Sachet and to the police. |
| Recovery agent asking a fee | A second scam. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Believing "it won't happen to me".** Frauds succeed through emotion, not ignorance. Habits protect everyone.
- **Keeping quiet after a loss.** Report fast and tell family; silence helps the fraudster.
- **Protecting only yourself.** Parents, grandparents and teenagers are targeted too. Brief them.

tasks.detail: **Proof to record:** Your completed checklist, the incident log template ready, the family code and briefing notes, saved in 15 Scams.

sections.title: FIN-M15-L01: Investment scams: Ponzi schemes, MLM, fake apps and finfluencers
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Recognise the patterns of Ponzi schemes, pyramid MLMs, fake trading apps and unregistered tipsters, and check any offer against official registers before parting with money. **Time:** about 2 hours (30 minutes reading, 30 minutes resources, 60 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

Kerala has seen large investment frauds that ruined thousands of families, some running for years with apparently steady payments. News reports describe victims of the **Highrich** case in Kasaragod still waiting for justice ([Onmanorama headline, December 2024](https://onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2024/12/20/high-rich-scam-kasaragod-victims-wait-for-justice.html)) and the High Court criticising inaction in the **₹2,000 crore Popular Finance** case ([Onmanorama headline, November 2025](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2025/11/12/kerala-high-court-popular-finance-scam.amp.html)). The people who lost money were not foolish; the schemes were designed to look trustworthy.

### Ponzi schemes

A **Ponzi scheme** pays "returns" to earlier investors from the money of newer ones. It works only while new money keeps coming, then collapses. Signs:

- **High, steady, "guaranteed" returns**, such as 2–5% a month, regardless of markets
- **Rewards for bringing in others**
- Vague explanations: "trading", "gold", "crypto", "foreign projects"
- **Pressure and secrecy:** "limited slots", "don't tell the bank"
- **Early payouts arrive on time** to build trust, often through people you know

India's **Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019** bans deposit schemes that aren't registered or regulated; its rules were notified to act against Ponzi schemes ([Moneylife headline](https://www.moneylife.in/article/govt-notifies-rules-for-banning-ponzi-schemes-unregulated-deposits-under-buds-act/59448.html)). RBI's **Sachet** portal lets you check lists of entities registered with different regulators and file a complaint ([RBI Sachet](https://sachet.rbi.org.in/)).

### Pyramid schemes dressed as MLM

Real direct selling earns from **selling products to real customers**. A pyramid scheme earns mainly from **recruiting people who pay to join**. The Consumer Protection (Direct Selling) Rules, 2021 prohibit direct sellers from promoting pyramid schemes or money circulation schemes, or from persuading people to buy on the promise that they can recover the price by recruiting others ([Moneylife, December 2021](https://moneylife.in/article/indian-govt-bans-pyramid-or-mlm-schemes-under-new-consumer-protection-rules/65986.html)). Ask: "If no one new joined, would anyone still buy the product at this price?"

### Fake trading apps, tip groups and finfluencers

A very common pattern now: a WhatsApp or Telegram group shares "expert" stock or crypto tips, then asks you to install an app or join an "institutional account". The app shows huge profits; when you try to withdraw, you are asked for a "tax" or "fee". The money was never invested. SEBI's investor website warns about **fake trading apps, "stock market guru" scams, pump-and-dump and dabba trading** ([SEBI investor site](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/)).

- Anyone giving paid investment advice or stock recommendations must be **registered with SEBI**; check the [list of registered investment advisers](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/other/OtherAction.do?doRecognisedFpi=yes&intmId=13) and SEBI's guidance ([SEBI](https://www.sebi.gov.in/media/press-releases/jun-2016/sebi-cautions-public-to-deal-with-only-sebi-registered-investment-advisers-and-research-analysts_32627.html)).
- SEBI-regulated firms can't be associated with unregistered finfluencers who give advice or claim returns ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/personal-finance/investment/story/sebi-tweaks-regulations-for-finfluencers-removes-content-of-over-15000-unregulated-entities-443789-2024-08-31)).
- Registered intermediaries collect money through **@valid UPI handles**, and **SEBI Check** verifies a UPI ID or bank account before you pay ([Moneylife](https://www.moneylife.in/article/sebi-launches-at-valid-upi-handles-and-checking-tool-to-curb-payment-frauds/78469.html)).
- "Digital gold" and similar products sit outside SEBI's regulation ([Moneylife](https://moneylife.in/article/sebi-warns-against-investing-in-unregulated-digital-gold-and-egold-products/78789.html)).

### Five questions before any investment

1. **Who regulates it?** RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA or a state law? Check the register yourself.
2. **Can I explain how it makes money** in two sentences?
3. **Are returns promised?** Real investments can't promise high returns.
4. **Can I get my money out, and how?** Test small, and read the exit terms.
5. **Who benefits if I say yes today?** Urgency is a sales tool.

## Local example

**Anu's** aunt, Rajani, was invited to a "business opportunity" meeting at a hotel in Kozhikode. The company sold health supplements and promised that members earned "₹50,000 a month" by building a team. Joining cost ₹25,000 in products.

Anu and Rajani applied the tests. The products cost three times similar ones in shops, so almost nobody would buy them except new members; the presentation spent 5 minutes on products and 50 on recruitment; and the "income proof" was screenshots, not tax returns. Under the 2021 Direct Selling Rules, a scheme like that, which depends on recruitment, is the kind of pyramid structure direct sellers are banned from promoting.

Rajani didn't join. Two of her friends did and lost most of their ₹25,000 in unsold products within a year. "The meeting felt like a celebration," Rajani said. "That was the trick."

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [SEBI investor website: guides and fraud warnings](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/) | SEBI's warnings on fake trading apps, "stock market guru" scams, pump and dump and dabba trading | 20 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Moneylife: pyramid and money-circulation schemes banned under consumer rules (December 2021)](https://moneylife.in/article/indian-govt-bans-pyramid-or-mlm-schemes-under-new-consumer-protection-rules/65986.html) | What the 2021 Direct Selling Rules prohibit | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [RBI Sachet: complain about illegal deposit schemes, check registered entities](https://sachet.rbi.org.in/) | RBI Sachet: registered entities and how to complain | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [SEBI: list of registered investment advisers (search by name or number)](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/other/OtherAction.do?doRecognisedFpi=yes&intmId=13) | Practise searching the SEBI adviser list | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [NCFE: free basic financial education course (e-LMS, about 5 hours)](https://ncfe.org.in/?p=430) | The e-LMS module on scams and frauds | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Do the spot-the-scam exercise in the template: for each message, write "scam" or "not a scam" and the red flags, before reading the answers.
2. List every investment offer, group or "opportunity" you or your family have been approached with in the last year.
3. Run the five questions on each, and check the regulator's register where relevant (SEBI list, RBI Sachet).
4. Leave or report any group that gives paid tips without registration.
5. Write your personal investment-scam rule in one sentence.

**Proof to record:** Your answers to the spot-the-scam exercise, the five-question check of real offers and your rule, saved in 15 Scams.

## Template: spot the scam (cover the answers, then check)

```
A. WhatsApp: "Join our VIP stock group. Our analyst gives 5% daily profit. 2,300 members earning. Install this app to trade with our institutional account."
   Answer: Fake trading app and unregistered tipster: guaranteed daily profit, an unknown app, no SEBI registration. SEBI warns about exactly these.
B. A relative: "Put ₹1 lakh in this company. It pays 4% every month, and you get ₹5,000 for every friend who joins."
   Answer: Ponzi pattern: high fixed monthly returns plus recruitment rewards. 4% a month is about 60% a year compounded.
C. SMS: "Your KSEB connection will be disconnected tonight at 9.30 pm. Call 98XXXXXXXX immediately."
   Answer: Phishing by urgency: utilities don't send such SMS from personal numbers. Check through the official app or office.
D. Video call from a "CBI officer" in uniform: "A parcel in your name has drugs. You are under digital arrest. Transfer money for verification."
   Answer: "Digital arrest" fraud: agencies don't arrest people on video calls. Hang up, call 1930.
E. Instagram ad: "Earn ₹3,000 a day liking YouTube videos. Small deposit to unlock higher tasks."
   Answer: Task scam: small payouts first, then deposits that never come back.
F. A KSFE branch notice about a new chitty, with the official chitty rules and a registered agreement.
   Answer: Not a scam: a regulated, government-owned institution with written terms. Still compare it as a loan or saving (FIN-M09-L07).
```

## Template: five-question investment check

```
Offer: ____  From: ____
1. Regulator and registration number (checked myself): ____
2. How it makes money, in two sentences: ____
3. Returns promised? Yes / No (if yes: walk away)
4. How I get my money out, and test result: ____
5. Who benefits if I say yes today? ____
Decision: ____
```

## Common mistakes

- **Trusting because a relative or friend invested.** Ponzi schemes spread through trust; early payouts are bait. Check the regulator, not the person.
- **Believing screenshots of profits.** Screenshots are easy to fake and never show the losers.
- **Paying a "withdrawal fee" to get money out.** Real platforms don't ask for fees to release your own money. Stop and report.
- **Staying silent after a loss.** Report quickly; it helps police stop the scheme and protects others.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. A scheme pays 3% a month, guaranteed, plus bonuses for recruits. What is it most likely to be?
    - A) A Ponzi scheme
    - B) An index fund
    - C) A government bond
    - D) A bank FD
2. Under the 2021 Direct Selling Rules, what can't direct sellers do?
    - A) Have customers
    - B) Promote pyramid or money circulation schemes
    - C) Sell products
    - D) Give receipts
3. An app shows big profits but asks for a "tax" before you can withdraw. What should you do?
    - A) Pay quickly before profits disappear
    - B) Recruit friends to cover it
    - C) Borrow to pay the fee
    - D) Stop paying and report it
4. How can you check whether someone giving paid stock advice is genuine?
    - A) Ask for profit screenshots
    - B) Search SEBI's list of registered investment advisers
    - C) Count their followers
    - D) Trust their certificate photo

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** SEBI's fraud warnings, the Direct Selling Rules, RBI Sachet, the SEBI adviser list and the NCFE scams module

sections.title: FIN-M15-L02: Payment frauds: UPI and OTP tricks, phishing and "digital arrest"
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Recognise the main payment frauds in India, including "digital arrest", and set up habits and settings that stop them, for yourself and your family. **Time:** about 2 hours (30 minutes reading, 25 minutes resources, 65 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

Payment fraudsters rarely hack anything. They **persuade you** to send money, approve a request, share a code or install an app. The script changes; the tricks stay the same: **urgency, fear, authority, greed and kindness**.

### Common frauds and the truth that defeats each

| The trick | What they say | The truth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fake KYC update | "Your account/SIM/electricity will be blocked today. Update KYC at this link." | Banks and utilities never ask through links from unknown numbers. Use the official app or office. |
| "Refund" by QR or UPI request | "Scan this QR to receive your refund." | Scanning a QR or entering your PIN only sends money. You never need your PIN to receive. |
| Fake customer care | A number found by search or social media | Use only numbers from the official website, app or passbook. |
| Remote access apps | "Install this app so I can help you." | Screen-sharing lets them see your OTPs and apps. Never install apps on a caller's instruction. |
| APK files on WhatsApp | "Traffic fine", "wedding invitation", "bank update" as an .apk file | Never install app files from messages; only from the official app store. |
| Task and job scams | "Earn by liking videos or rating hotels. Deposit to unlock higher tasks." | Real jobs don't ask you to pay. Small early payouts are bait. |
| Marketplace scams | A "buyer" or "army officer" sends a QR to "pay you" | QR codes are for paying, not receiving. |
| SIM swap | Your phone suddenly loses network | Contact your mobile operator immediately; someone may be getting your OTPs. |

### "Digital arrest"

In a **digital arrest** fraud, callers pretend to be from the CBI, police, customs, ED or even judges, often by video call with uniforms and fake offices. They claim you or a relative are linked to drugs or money laundering, keep you on camera "under arrest" for hours, and demand money transfers to "clear your name". India's Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) issued an advisory: **"CBI/Police/Custom/ED/Judges DO NOT arrest you on video call"**; don't panic, and report on **1930** or **cybercrime.gov.in** ([ETV Bharat, October 2024](https://www.etvbharat.com/en/!bharat/cbi-ed-police-dont-arrest-people-through-video-calls-indian-cyber-crime-coordination-centre-enn24100602996)).

**There is no such thing as a digital arrest in Indian law.** Hang up, and call a family member and 1930.

### Report attempts before any loss: Chakshu

If you receive a suspicious call, SMS or WhatsApp message but **haven't lost money**, you can report it on **Chakshu**, a facility on the Department of Telecommunications' Sanchar Saathi portal, which acts against numbers used for fraud. If money has already gone, use **1930** or the cyber crime portal instead ([Factly](https://factly.in/explainer-government-launches-chakshu-to-report-sms-call-or-whatsapp-messages-attempting-to-commit-fraud/amp)).

### Settings and habits that block most frauds

1. **A separate, low-balance account for UPI:** keep most money in an account that isn't linked to UPI apps.
2. **Transaction alerts on** (Module 4), and a **daily UPI limit** that fits your needs.
3. **Two-step verification** on email and important apps; a screen lock; app locks on payment apps.
4. **Type addresses yourself:** bank websites end in **.bank.in** ([Business Standard headline](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/finance/news/rbi-asks-banks-to-complete-migration-to-bank-in-domain-by-october-31-2025-125042201515_1.html)).
5. **Pause and verify:** any message with urgency, fear or a prize gets a 10-minute pause and a call to an official number or a family member.
6. **Never share** OTPs, PINs, passwords or CVVs, with anyone.

## Local example

**Joseph**, Anu's neighbour, got a video call from a "Mumbai Police officer" who said a parcel in Joseph's name contained drugs and that a "CBI judge" would decide his case online. Joseph was told not to tell anyone and to stay on camera. After an hour of fear, the "officer" asked him to transfer his FD money to a "verification account" that would be returned after the inquiry.

Joseph remembered the fraud response card on his kitchen cupboard (FIN-M04-L02): 1930. He said he needed the bathroom, called his daughter from the landline, and she told him what the I4C advisory says: real agencies don't arrest people on video calls. He hung up. Then they reported the number on Chakshu, because no money had been lost.

His daughter later set up two protections: his FD account is no longer linked to any UPI app, and his UPI account holds only his monthly expenses.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [ETV Bharat: I4C says CBI, ED and police don't arrest people on video calls (October 2024)](https://www.etvbharat.com/en/!bharat/cbi-ed-police-dont-arrest-people-through-video-calls-indian-cyber-crime-coordination-centre-enn24100602996) | I4C's "digital arrest" advisory | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Factly: Chakshu, to report fraud calls, SMS and WhatsApp messages](https://factly.in/explainer-government-launches-chakshu-to-report-sms-call-or-whatsapp-messages-attempting-to-commit-fraud/amp) | What Chakshu is for, and when to use 1930 instead | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [RBI: customer liability in unauthorised electronic transactions](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/FS_Notification.aspx?Id=11040) | Revise your rights after an unauthorised transaction | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [RBI: Financial Education (messages, films, games, downloads)](https://rbi.org.in/financialeducation/) | RBI's Financial Awareness Messages on safe digital banking | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Check your payment set-up: which accounts are linked to UPI apps? Consider keeping savings in an account that isn't.
2. Set or lower your daily UPI limit in your bank app or UPI app.
3. Check two-step verification on your email and screen locks on your phone; turn them on if off.
4. Fill in the scam-proof habits checklist for yourself.
5. Teach one family member (ideally an older one) the "digital arrest" truth and the 10-minute pause, and write what you discussed.

**Proof to record:** Your completed scam-proof habits checklist, a screenshot of your UPI limit or account set-up (numbers covered) and a note on the family conversation, saved in 15 Scams.

## Template: scam-proof habits checklist

```
[ ] Savings kept in an account not linked to any UPI app
[ ] Daily UPI limit set to what I really need: ₹____
[ ] Transaction alerts (SMS and email) on for every account
[ ] Two-step verification on email and important apps
[ ] Screen lock and app locks on
[ ] I never install apps or .apk files because a caller or message tells me to
[ ] I never scan a QR code or enter a PIN to "receive" money
[ ] I find customer care numbers only on official websites, apps or passbooks
[ ] I pause 10 minutes and verify when a message has urgency, fear or a prize
[ ] I know: no agency arrests anyone on a video call
[ ] I know: 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in if money is lost; Chakshu for attempts
```

## Common mistakes

- **Thinking frauds only target the careless.** They target fear and kindness. Habits and settings protect you when emotions run high.
- **Keeping all savings in the UPI-linked account.** A low-balance UPI account limits the damage of any mistake.
- **Engaging with scammers to "teach them a lesson".** Hang up and report; they are skilled at pulling you back in.
- **Not telling elderly family members.** Older people are targeted most; a 10-minute conversation can save their savings.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. A video caller in police uniform says you are under "digital arrest". What is true?
    - A) No agency arrests anyone on a video call; hang up and call 1930
    - B) You need a lawyer on the call
    - C) You should transfer money for verification
    - D) You must stay on camera
2. You got a suspicious SMS but lost no money. Where can you report it?
    - A) Only the bank
    - B) Chakshu on the Sanchar Saathi portal
    - C) Nowhere
    - D) The income tax portal
3. A "buyer" sends you a QR code to pay you for your old phone. What should you do?
    - A) Install their app
    - B) Send your OTP
    - C) Refuse; QR codes are for paying, not receiving
    - D) Scan it and enter your PIN
4. Which set-up limits damage from payment fraud?
    - A) All savings in the UPI account
    - B) Sharing your PIN with family
    - C) A separate low-balance account for UPI, with a daily limit
    - D) Alerts turned off

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The I4C digital arrest advisory, Chakshu, your liability rights and RBI's awareness messages
- **Action:** Lock down your payment set-up, complete the habits checklist and brief one family member. It is done when your proof is saved: your completed scam-proof habits checklist, a screenshot of your UPI limit or account set-up (numbers covered) and a note on the family conversation, saved in 15 Scams.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** The I4C advisory says CBI, police, customs, ED and judges don't arrest people on video calls.
2. **B.** Chakshu is for suspected fraud communications; 1930 is for money already lost.
3. **C.** Scanning and entering a PIN sends your money out.
4. **C.** If something goes wrong, only a small amount is exposed.
