sections.title: FIN-M15-L03: Report fast, recover what you can, and protect your family
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Know exactly where to report each kind of fraud, keep the evidence that helps, avoid "recovery" scams, and run a family scam briefing. **Time:** about 1 hour 30 minutes (20 minutes reading, 20 minutes resources, 50 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Where to report what

| What happened | Report to | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Money lost through UPI, card, net banking or an online fraud | **1930** (24 hours) and **cybercrime.gov.in**; then block and report to your bank in writing | Fast reports give the best chance to freeze money in the fraudster's account; your bank liability depends on how fast you report (FIN-M04-L02) |
| A suspicious call, SMS or WhatsApp message, no money lost | **Chakshu** on the Sanchar Saathi portal | Helps block numbers used for fraud |
| A company taking deposits illegally, a Ponzi or chit fraud | **RBI Sachet** complaint and the police | Brings regulators and state authorities in |
| A problem with a SEBI-registered broker, adviser or fund | **SEBI SCORES**, after complaining to the entity | The entity must respond within 21 days |
| A bank or NBFC doesn't resolve your complaint | **RBI Ombudsman** (cms.rbi.org.in) | Free, after 30 days or a rejection |
| An insurance problem | **Bima Bharosa**, then the **Insurance Ombudsman** | Free escalation (FIN-M07-L05) |
| Threats, harassment, large losses | **Police station** (FIR) as well as the above | For investigation and legal action |

Sources: [Kerala Police on 1930](https://ps.keralapolice.gov.in/ernakulamruralcyber-ps/notifications/National-Cyber-Crime-Reporting-Helpline-No-1930-3338), [National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal](https://cybercrime.gov.in/), [Chakshu](https://factly.in/explainer-government-launches-chakshu-to-report-sms-call-or-whatsapp-messages-attempting-to-commit-fraud/amp), [RBI Sachet](https://sachet.rbi.org.in/), [SEBI SCORES](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/sebi_scores.html), [RBI Ombudsman scheme](https://www.canarabank.bank.in/documents/d/guest/salient-features-of-the-scheme-2026), [Bima Bharosa](https://bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in/).

### The first hour: speed beats everything

Kerala Police says reporting online financial scams promptly is crucial, so that investigators can gather evidence and act before it is destroyed ([Kerala Police](https://ps.keralapolice.gov.in/ernakulamruralcyber-ps/notifications/National-Cyber-Crime-Reporting-Helpline-No-1930-3338)). Call 1930 first, then block your card or UPI, then file online and in writing.

### Evidence to keep

- Screenshots of messages, chats, call logs, profiles, websites and apps (with the URL)
- Transaction IDs (UTR numbers), dates, amounts, the receiver's UPI ID or account
- Any names, numbers and links the fraudster used
- Your complaint and acknowledgement numbers

Don't delete chats in anger or shame; they are evidence.

### Recovery scams: the second fraud

After a loss, victims are often contacted by "recovery agents", "cyber lawyers" or even fake police officers who promise to get the money back for a fee. Genuine police and regulators don't charge for investigations. Anyone asking for a fee to recover lost money is almost certainly running a second scam.

### Shame is the fraudster's best friend

Victims often stay silent, which lets frauds continue and stops recovery. Fraud happens to doctors, engineers, bank staff and police officers. Tell your family, report, and use your experience to warn others.

### A family scam briefing

Once a year, or whenever a new scam is in the news, spend 20 minutes with your family:

1. Share the three rules: **never share codes, never install apps for callers, never pay to "receive" or "recover" money**.
2. Explain "digital arrest" and the five-question investment check.
3. Agree a **family code**: anyone who gets a scary call or a "great scheme" calls a named family member before doing anything.
4. Put the fraud response card and 1930 where everyone can see them.

## Local example

**Fathima** lost ₹18,000 when she paid an advance to a fake "furniture supplier" she found on social media. She noticed within an hour, when the seller's profile vanished.

She called **1930** at once and gave the UTR number and the receiver's UPI ID; the call centre registered her complaint and asked her to complete it on the cyber crime portal, which she did within the hour. She reported the transaction to her bank in writing. Some days later, the police informed her that part of the money had been frozen in the receiving account; she received ₹11,000 back through the process the police and bank followed.

Two days after her loss, a "cyber recovery expert" messaged her offering to recover the rest for a ₹3,000 fee. She recognised the second scam, reported the number on Chakshu, and told the story at her family's next briefing so her cousins wouldn't fall for either trick.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Kerala Police: 1930, the national cyber crime helpline](https://ps.keralapolice.gov.in/ernakulamruralcyber-ps/notifications/National-Cyber-Crime-Reporting-Helpline-No-1930-3338) | Kerala Police on the 1930 helpline and prompt reporting | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Factly: Chakshu, to report fraud calls, SMS and WhatsApp messages](https://factly.in/explainer-government-launches-chakshu-to-report-sms-call-or-whatsapp-messages-attempting-to-commit-fraud/amp) | When to use Chakshu and when to use 1930 | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [RBI Sachet: complain about illegal deposit schemes, check registered entities](https://sachet.rbi.org.in/) | Filing a complaint on RBI Sachet | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [SEBI investor website: SCORES complaints](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/sebi_scores.html) | How SEBI SCORES works | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [NCFE: free basic financial education course (e-LMS, about 5 hours)](https://ncfe.org.in/?p=430) | Finish the NCFE scams and frauds module and its quiz | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Save 1930 in your phone as "Cyber Fraud Helpline" and bookmark the official portals from this lesson.
2. Make a **Scam Check** tab with the incident log template, ready to use.
3. Write your family code: who family members should call before acting on a scary call or a "scheme".
4. Hold a 20-minute family scam briefing using the four points, and write who attended and what questions came up.
5. Put the fraud response card and 1930 in a visible place at home.

**Proof to record:** The incident log ready in your Scam Check tab, your family code and notes from the family briefing, saved in 15 Scams.

## Template: incident log (fill in immediately if something happens)

```
Date and time noticed: ____
What happened (short): ____
Amount and transaction IDs (UTR): ____
Receiver's UPI ID / account / phone / website: ____
1930 called at (time): ____  Complaint number: ____
cybercrime.gov.in acknowledgement: ____
Bank informed at (time, how): ____  Card/UPI blocked: Yes / No
Other reports (Chakshu, Sachet, SCORES, police FIR): ____
Evidence saved (screenshots folder): ____
Follow-up dates: ____
```

## Template: family scam briefing card

```
OUR FAMILY RULES
1. We never share OTPs, PINs or passwords. With anyone.
2. We never install apps or files because a caller or message says so.
3. We never pay to receive money, release profits or recover losses.
4. No agency arrests anyone on a video call.
5. Before acting on a scary call or a "great scheme", call: ____ (family code person)
LOST MONEY? Call 1930 at once, then the bank. Report at cybercrime.gov.in.
```

## Common mistakes

- **Waiting before reporting.** Every hour matters for freezing money. Call 1930 first.
- **Deleting chats out of shame.** They are the evidence investigators need.
- **Paying "recovery agents".** It is a second scam. Real investigations don't charge you.
- **Briefing family only once.** Scams change; repeat the briefing yearly and when new tricks appear.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. You lost money through a UPI fraud an hour ago. What is the first step?
    - A) Call 1930
    - B) Pay a recovery agent
    - C) Post on social media
    - D) Wait a day to see if it comes back
2. A company in your town takes deposits promising 3% a month. Where can you complain?
    - A) Nowhere
    - B) RBI Sachet and the police
    - C) SEBI SCORES only
    - D) Bima Bharosa
3. Someone offers to recover your lost money for a fee. What is it most likely to be?
    - A) A bank refund
    - B) A second scam
    - C) The police
    - D) A legal requirement
4. Which evidence is most useful after a payment fraud?
    - A) Only your memory
    - B) Transaction IDs (UTR), the receiver's UPI ID or account, screenshots
    - C) Your credit score
    - D) Your PAN card

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The 1930 helpline, Chakshu, RBI Sachet, SEBI SCORES and the NCFE scams module
- **Action:** Prepare your incident log, write a family code and hold a family scam briefing. It is done when your proof is saved: the incident log ready in your Scam Check tab, your family code and notes from the family briefing, saved in 15 Scams.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** Fast reporting gives the best chance of freezing the money.
2. **B.** Sachet handles complaints about illegal deposit-taking; police can act too.
3. **B.** Genuine investigations don't charge victims.
4. **B.** Investigators trace money through transaction details.

sections.title: Module 16: Growing income
sections.summary: Use the biggest lever in personal finance, your income, by choosing one realistic path for the next 90 days and setting money rules so extra income becomes progress.
sections.content:
## Overview

This module is deliberately short, because the skills live in the other courses in this app: Practical Entrepreneurship for a business, Practical Social Media Marketing and the Free AI Generalist Course for freelancing, and your PSC preparation for a government job. Here you choose one path, plan a small real test, and connect it to your budget, tax and goals.

The result is a one-page income growth plan, which becomes part of your final financial plan.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Choose one income path that fits your time and skills
- Plan a 90-day test with a rupee target
- Set money rules for extra income: holding account, tax set-aside, raise rule
- Judge courses and tools by their payback, and avoid "get rich" traps

## Time

About 2 hours in total: 1 hour 30 minutes of lessons and 30 minutes for the module project. Part-time: week 29.

## Lessons

1. FIN-M16-L01: Growing your income: the biggest lever, used wisely (about 1 hour 30 minutes)

## Module project: My income growth plan

1. Finish the one-page plan from FIN-M16-L01.
2. Put the 90-day review date in your calendar.
3. Add the expected extra income to your Cash Flow tab as a separate line, marked "planned".

**Proof to record:** Your one-page income growth plan and the review date, saved in 16 Income.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Path | None chosen | Several half-chosen | One path with a clear reason |
| Test | Vague | A goal without numbers | A 90-day test with a rupee target |
| Money rules | None | Some | Holding account, tax set-aside and raise rule written |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Write the path, the 90-day test and the money rules in five lines.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| The biggest lever on a small income | Growing income. |
| Payback of a course | Cost ÷ extra monthly income it should bring. |
| First home for freelance income | A holding account, with tax and costs set aside. |
| Not an income plan | Pyramid schemes, deposit-based "tasks" and F&O trading. |
| Where to learn earning skills in this app | Entrepreneurship (ENT-M05, M08, M09), Social Media Marketing (SMM-M15), AI Generalist (Level 1, Capstone). |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Waiting for the perfect idea.** A small real test beats a perfect plan on paper.
- **Letting side income disappear into lifestyle.** Apply the raise rule from the first payment.

sections.title: FIN-M16-L01: Growing your income: the biggest lever, used wisely
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Choose one realistic way to grow your income in the next year, using the other courses in this app, and set money rules so extra income becomes progress, not lifestyle. **Time:** about 1 hour 30 minutes (20 minutes reading, 20 minutes resources, 50 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

On a small income, cutting costs helps, but only up to a point: you can't save more than you earn. **Growing income is the biggest lever in personal finance.** This short module points you to the courses in this app that teach the skills, and adds the money rules that make extra income count.

### Four paths, and where this app teaches them

| Path | What it takes | Where to learn it in this app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A government job through Kerala PSC | Steady preparation; then Module 14 of this course for the money side | Your PSC study plan; FIN-M14 |
| Freelancing with a skill | A skill clients pay for, a portfolio, a price and a way to find clients | Social Media Marketing course: packages and pricing (SMM-M15-L01), finding clients (SMM-M15-L02), contracts and reports (SMM-M15-L03); Free AI Generalist Course: Level 1 and the Capstone on first clients |
| Your own small business | A tested idea, pricing, bookkeeping, registrations | Practical Entrepreneurship: pricing (ENT-M05-L03), bookkeeping and cash flow (ENT-M08-L01), registrations in Kerala (ENT-M09-L02), funding (ENT-M08-L04) |
| Growing in a job | Skills, results you can show, and asking for more | Any course that builds a skill your employer values |

### The money rules for extra income

1. **Separate it:** freelance or business money goes into a holding account (FIN-M03-L04), with tax and costs set aside from every payment.
2. **Know the tax:** small freelance incomes often owe no income tax under the new regime, but presumptive taxation, TDS refunds, advance tax and the GST threshold apply as income grows ([section 58](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-58-144), [GST registration](https://cbic-gst.gov.in/pdf/press-release/registrtn-gst-regime.pdf); FIN-M10-L05).
3. **Use the raise rule:** at least half of any increase in income goes to your goals and emergency fund (Module 1).
4. **Budget for learning:** a course or tool that raises income can be a good use of money; calculate the payback first.

> **Payback in months = cost of the course or tool ÷ extra income per month it should bring**

A ₹6,000 course that realistically adds ₹2,000 a month pays back in 3 months. A ₹60,000 "trading mastery" course promising ₹1 lakh a month is a red flag, not an investment (Module 15).

### What doesn't grow income

- **"Business opportunities"** that need you to pay to join and recruit others (pyramid schemes, Module 15)
- **Task and "work from home" schemes** that ask for deposits
- **Trading futures and options as a "job"**: about 91% of individual traders lost money in 2024-25 ([SEBI study](https://moneylife.in/article/91-percentage-of-retail-traders-lost-money-in-derivatives-losses-in-fo-surged-41-percentage-to-rs105-lakh-crore-in-fy2425-sebi-study/77613.html))
- **Borrowing to start** something you haven't tested with real customers

### Start small and test

Pick **one** path for the next 90 days. Do the smallest real test: one paying client, one product sold, one certification finished. Measure the result in rupees, then decide whether to grow it.

## Local example

**Anu** earns about ₹14,000 a month from tuition while preparing for PSC exams. She looked at the four paths and chose one for the next 90 days, without hurting her PSC preparation: **freelance social media management for local shops**, using the Social Media Marketing course she had started.

Her 90-day plan: finish the course's earning module (SMM-M15), offer a ₹3,000-a-month starter package to two shops in Kakkattil (one already knew her from tuition), and track hours so her PSC study time stayed protected. Money rules: a second savings account as her holding account; 10% of every payment set aside for tax until she checks her position in FIN-M10-L05; half of the extra income to her emergency fund until it is full.

After 90 days she had one paying client (₹3,000 a month) and a case study. Her income rose by about 20%; her savings rate rose by more, because the new income followed her rules from day one.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [NCFE: free basic financial education course (e-LMS, about 5 hours)](https://ncfe.org.in/?p=430) | Revise the managing income and expenditure module with extra income in mind | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Income-tax Act, 2025, section 58: presumptive taxation for small businesses and professionals](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/section-58-144) | How small freelance and business income can be taxed (presumptive scheme) | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [CBIC: registration under GST (PDF)](https://cbic-gst.gov.in/pdf/press-release/registrtn-gst-regime.pdf) | When GST registration becomes necessary | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [Moneylife: SEBI study, 91% of individual F&O traders lost money in 2024-25](https://moneylife.in/article/91-percentage-of-retail-traders-lost-money-in-derivatives-losses-in-fo-surged-41-percentage-to-rs105-lakh-crore-in-fy2425-sebi-study/77613.html) | Why trading derivatives is not an income plan | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Choose one income path for the next 90 days and write why it fits your time, skills and PSC plans.
2. Open the matching course and module in this app and note the lessons you will use.
3. Write the smallest real test you can do in 90 days, with a rupee target.
4. Set your money rules for the extra income: holding account, tax set-aside, raise rule.
5. Calculate the payback of any course or tool you plan to pay for.

**Proof to record:** Your one-page income growth plan with the 90-day test, money rules and payback calculation, saved in 16 Income.

## Template: income growth plan (one page)

```
Path chosen: ____   Why it fits me: ____
Course and lessons in this app: ____
90-day test: ____ (e.g. 2 paying clients at ₹3,000 a month)
Hours per week, protected around PSC study: ____
Money rules: holding account ____ | tax set-aside ___% | ___% of extra income to goals
Spending on learning or tools: ₹____ ; payback =cost/extra_monthly_income = ____ months
Review date: ____  Result in rupees: ____  Next step: ____
```

## Common mistakes

- **Chasing several paths at once.** One focused 90-day test teaches more than four half-started ideas.
- **Spending extra income before it is regular.** Let extra income follow your rules for a few months first.
- **Paying for "get rich" courses.** Calculate the payback; promises of huge incomes are a warning sign.
- **Forgetting tax on side income.** Set aside a share of every payment and check your position in Module 10.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. A ₹9,000 course should realistically add ₹3,000 a month. What is its payback period?
    - A) 1 month
    - B) 9 months
    - C) 3 months
    - D) 27 months
2. Where should freelance income go first?
    - A) Straight into spending
    - B) Into F&O trading
    - C) Into a chitty
    - D) A holding account, with tax and costs set aside
3. Which of these is NOT a real way to grow income?
    - A) Learning a skill clients pay for
    - B) Paying to join a scheme that rewards recruiting
    - C) Earning a promotion with better skills
    - D) Testing a small business with real customers
4. What is the course's rule for extra income?
    - A) Spend it all to enjoy it
    - B) At least half goes to goals and the emergency fund
    - C) Invest it all in one stock
    - D) Keep it secret

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The NCFE income module, presumptive taxation, the GST threshold and SEBI's F&O study
- **Action:** Write a one-page income growth plan with a 90-day test and money rules. It is done when your proof is saved: your one-page income growth plan with the 90-day test, money rules and payback calculation, saved in 16 Income.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** ₹9,000 ÷ ₹3,000 = 3 months.
2. **D.** The salary system from FIN-M03-L04 keeps irregular income under control.
3. **B.** Recruitment-based schemes are pyramids (Module 15).
4. **B.** The raise rule turns extra income into progress.

sections.title: Module 17: Capstone: your complete personal financial plan
sections.summary: Bring everything together: a signed Investment Policy Statement, a one-page financial plan with live numbers and dated actions, and a yearly review routine that keeps it all working.
sections.content:
## Overview

Over 31 weeks you have built every part of a personal financial plan on your own money: a budget system, a net-worth tracker, an emergency fund, a debt plan, insurance checks, investment rules, a tax checklist, retirement and goal plans, an estate file and scam-proof habits. The capstone turns those parts into a system you can run for the rest of your life.

Write your Investment Policy Statement, build the one-page plan that pulls numbers from every tab, and run your first yearly review. Then finish the course with the final self-assessment.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Write and sign a personal Investment Policy Statement
- Build a one-page financial plan with linked numbers and dated actions
- Run a complete yearly money review and keep a review log
- Schedule monthly, quarterly and yearly money routines
- Explain your plan to the people it affects

## Time

About 8 hours in total: 6 hours of lessons and 2 hours for the module project. Part-time: weeks 30–31.

## Lessons

1. FIN-M17-L01: Write your Investment Policy Statement (about 2 hours)
2. FIN-M17-L02: Your one-page financial plan (about 2 hours 30 minutes)
3. FIN-M17-L03: The yearly money review: keeping the system running (about 1 hour 30 minutes)

## Module project: My complete personal financial plan

1. Check that every tab in your Money Workbook is filled in and dated: Expenses, Baseline, Values, Goals, Net Worth, Cash Flow, Budget, Accounts, Emergency, Debts, Insurance, Calculators, Allocation, Funds, Tax, Big Goals, Retirement, Documents, Pay Slip (if relevant), Scam Check, Plan and Review.
2. Attach your signed IPS and your one-page plan.
3. Present the plan to your money buddy or family in 15 minutes: where you started (your week 0 snapshot), where you are, and the next 12 months.
4. Write a short reflection: the three most valuable changes the course made to your money, and one thing still to improve.
5. Do the final self-assessment and toolkit checklist on the next page.

**Proof to record:** Your complete Money Workbook (downloaded copy), signed IPS, one-page plan and reflection, saved in 17 Plan.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Completeness | Several parts missing | Most parts present | Every part present, dated and consistent |
| IPS | Not written | Written but vague | Signed, specific, with crash and windfall rules |
| One-page plan | None | Typed numbers, no actions | Linked numbers and dated actions in the calendar |
| Routine | None | Intentions | Monthly, quarterly and yearly routines scheduled; review log started |
| Shared | Kept private | Mentioned | Presented to the people it affects |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Write the IPS with at least allocation, banned options and the crash rule (FIN-M17-L01).
- Fill in the one-page plan, even with some numbers typed (FIN-M17-L02).
- Book next year's review weekend (FIN-M17-L03).

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Investment Policy Statement | Your written investing rules: goals, profile, allocation, allowed and banned options, contributions, rebalancing, behaviour, review. |
| The crash rule | What you will do (and not do) when markets fall sharply, written in advance. |
| One-page plan | Key numbers linked from your workbook plus dated actions for 12 months. |
| Yearly review | One fixed month: numbers, protection, debt, goals, investing, tax and rules, estate, safety, income, plan. |
| Quarterly checks | Small savings rates, CAS, AIS and allocation drift. |
| Monthly check | The 30-minute money review with one decision. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Treating the plan as finished.** It is a living system; the review keeps it true.
- **Changing everything after the course.** Keep the routines simple enough to keep for decades.
- **Forgetting why you started.** Reread your week 0 three sentences at every yearly review.

sections.title: FIN-M17-L01: Write your Investment Policy Statement
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Write a one-to-two-page Investment Policy Statement: your goals, risk profile, target allocation, allowed and banned options, selection rules, contributions, rebalancing and behaviour rules, signed and dated. **Time:** about 2 hours (20 minutes reading, 20 minutes resources, 80 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

An **Investment Policy Statement (IPS)** is a short document of rules you write for yourself **when you are calm**, so you follow them when markets, friends or salespeople make you excited or afraid. Professional fund managers and pension funds use them. You need one more than they do, because nobody checks your decisions.

You already have almost everything from earlier modules. This lesson puts it in one place.

### The ten parts of a personal IPS

1. **Purpose:** what this money is for (your goals by horizon, from Modules 2, 11 and 12).
2. **Risk profile:** your capacity and tolerance scores and the profile you use (FIN-M08-L02).
3. **Target allocation** for each horizon, with allowed ranges (FIN-M08-L03).
4. **Allowed options** for each job: safety, income, growth, diversifiers (your Shortlist from Module 9).
5. **Banned options:** what you won't do, such as F&O trading, unregistered tips, unregulated "digital gold", schemes promising fixed high returns, borrowing to invest (Modules 9 and 15).
6. **Selection rules:** for example, direct plans only; index funds for core equity; an expense ratio limit; only SEBI-registered advisers paid by fee; check every product's regulator ([AMFI on direct plans](https://www.amfiindia.com/investor-corner/investor-center/Direct-Plan.html), [SEBI riskometer](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/riskometer.html)).
7. **Contributions:** monthly amounts, dates, accounts and the yearly step-up (Module 12).
8. **Rebalancing rule:** date, drift limit and "new money first" (FIN-M08-L03).
9. **Behaviour rules:** what you will do in a market fall ("nothing for 30 days, then follow the rebalancing rule"), with windfalls ("wait 30 days, then follow the allocation"), with tips ("check registration, then ignore"), with a new product ("five questions and 24 hours").
10. **Review:** when you will review the IPS (yearly), and the life events that trigger a review (marriage, job change, a big windfall), plus when you will consult a SEBI-registered investment adviser ([SEBI list](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/other/OtherAction.do?doRecognisedFpi=yes&intmId=13)).

### Keep it short and specific

Two pages at most. Every rule should be checkable: "Equity 50% ± 5%" is checkable; "moderate risk" is not. Sign and date it, and keep it in your Money Folder and on paper.

### The crash rule matters most

Markets fall sharply from time to time. People lose the most money not in the fall itself but by selling near the bottom and missing the recovery. Writing your crash rule now, with your long-term horizon in front of you, is the most valuable sentence in your IPS.

## Local example

**Anu's** IPS (summary of her two pages):

| Part | Anu's rule |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Emergency fund and short goals (safe); retirement from age 27 (long-term) |
| Profile | Balanced (capacity 10, tolerance 11) |
| Allocation, long-term money | Equity 50% (45–55%), debt 45% (PPF), gold 5% (gold ETF or fund) |
| Allowed | Post office RD and TD, bank FDs within ₹5 lakh per bank, PPF, a broad equity index fund (direct plan), a gold ETF or fund |
| Banned | F&O, tips from unregistered people, digital gold apps, private chitties, crypto, any scheme promising fixed high returns, loans to invest |
| Selection | Direct plans; index funds with low expense ratios and long tracking records; check the regulator every time |
| Contributions | ₹1,000 PPF and ₹1,000 index fund SIP monthly from the 5th; +10% every April |
| Rebalancing | 1 April each year; act if drift > 5 points; new money first |
| Crash rule | If markets fall 20% or more: do nothing for 30 days, keep the SIP going, then rebalance by rule |
| Review | Every April; also after a PSC job offer, marriage or any windfall over ₹50,000 |

She printed it, signed it, and asked her money buddy to sign as a witness, "so I'm embarrassed to break it".

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [AMFI: direct plans explained](https://www.amfiindia.com/investor-corner/investor-center/Direct-Plan.html) | Revise direct plans for your selection rules | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [SEBI investor website: riskometer](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/riskometer.html) | Revise the riskometer for your risk rules | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [SEBI investor website: guides and fraud warnings](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/) | Skim SEBI's investor guides for any rule you want to add | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Collect your inputs: Goals tab, risk profile, Allocation tab, the Shortlist from Module 9, your Retirement plan and your rules from Modules 9 and 15.
2. Write your IPS using the template, in your own words, with every rule checkable.
3. Write your crash rule and your windfall rule with special care.
4. Read it aloud to your money buddy or a family member and change anything that is unclear.
5. Sign and date it; save it in 17 Plan and keep a printed copy.
6. Set up or adjust the contributions it describes, if you haven't already.

**Proof to record:** Your signed and dated Investment Policy Statement (PDF or photo), saved in 17 Plan.

## Template: Investment Policy Statement

```
MY INVESTMENT POLICY STATEMENT    Name: ____    Date: ____    Next review: ____
1. PURPOSE: short goals (under 3 years): ____ | medium (3-7): ____ | long (over 7): ____
2. RISK PROFILE: capacity __/15, tolerance __/15 → profile: ____
3. TARGET ALLOCATION (long-term money): equity ___% (range __-__) | debt ___% | gold ___% | cash ___%
   Medium-term money: ____    Short-term money: safe options only
4. ALLOWED: safety ____ | income ____ | growth ____ | diversifiers ____
5. BANNED: ____ (e.g. F&O, unregistered tips, unregulated digital gold, schemes promising fixed high returns, borrowing to invest)
6. SELECTION RULES: direct plans [ ] expense ratio below ___% [ ] regulator checked [ ] advisers SEBI-registered and fee-only [ ]
7. CONTRIBUTIONS: ₹____ to ____ on the __th; ₹____ to ____ ; step-up ___% every ____
8. REBALANCING: every ____ ; if drift > ___ points; new money first
9. BEHAVIOUR: in a crash: ____ | windfalls: ____ | tips: ____ | new products: five questions + 24 hours
10. REVIEW: yearly in ____ ; also after: ____ ; consult a SEBI RIA when: ____
Signed: ____    Witness (optional): ____
```

## Common mistakes

- **Writing vague rules.** "Be careful" can't be checked. "Equity 50% ± 5%" can.
- **Copying someone else's IPS.** Your goals, profile and family are yours; the rules must be too.
- **Skipping the crash rule.** It is the rule you will need most, at the moment you least want to think.
- **Never reading it again.** Read it before every investment decision and at every yearly review.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What is an Investment Policy Statement?
    - A) Your written rules for investing, made calmly in advance
    - B) A bank statement
    - C) A list of hot stocks
    - D) A tax form
2. Which is a checkable IPS rule?
    - A) Take moderate risk
    - B) Invest wisely
    - C) Equity 50%, allowed range 45–55%
    - D) Avoid bad funds
3. Why write a crash rule in advance?
    - A) To pay less tax
    - B) Banks require it
    - C) Fear in a fall leads to selling near the bottom
    - D) Crashes never happen
4. Which belongs in the "banned" section for most beginners, per this course?
    - A) Post office deposits
    - B) PPF
    - C) F&O trading and schemes promising fixed high returns
    - D) Direct index funds

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Revision of direct plans, the riskometer and SEBI's investor guides
- **Action:** Write, sign and date your Investment Policy Statement. It is done when your proof is saved: your signed and dated Investment Policy Statement (PDF or photo), saved in 17 Plan.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** It guides decisions when emotions run high.
2. **C.** You can measure it and know when to act.
3. **C.** A rule written calmly beats a decision made in panic.
4. **C.** Modules 9 and 15 showed their risks.

sections.title: FIN-M17-L02: Your one-page financial plan
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Pull every module's work into a one-page financial plan with live numbers from your Money Workbook and a dated list of actions for the next 12 months. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (15 minutes reading, 15 minutes resources, 120 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

Your Money Workbook now holds everything: budget, net worth, goals, emergency fund, debts, insurance, allocation, tax, retirement, documents and more. A **one-page plan** puts the most important numbers and decisions where you, and your family, can see them at a glance.

### What goes on the page

| Section | What to show | Comes from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where I am | Net worth, liquid net worth, monthly take-home, savings rate | Modules 2 and 3 |
| Protection | Emergency fund (target, current, months covered); life, health and accident cover | Modules 5 and 7 |
| Debt | Total debt, payoff order, debt-free date, credit report checked on | Module 6 |
| Goals | Top goals with amounts, dates, monthly saving and progress | Modules 2, 11 and 12 |
| Investing | Allocation now vs target; IPS signed on; contributions | Modules 8, 9 and 17 |
| Tax | Regime, expected tax, due dates | Module 10 |
| Estate | Nominations checked on, will status, money file location | Module 13 |
| Safety | Scam-proof habits done, family briefing date | Module 15 |
| Income | 90-day income plan and result | Module 16 |
| Next 12 months | Five to eight dated actions | This lesson |

### Live numbers, not copies

Make a **Plan** tab whose numbers come from the other tabs by formula, so it stays current when you update them. In Google Sheets a reference to another tab looks like `='Net Worth'!I4`; in LibreOffice it looks like `=$'Net Worth'.I4`. The safest way in both is to type `=`, click the other tab's cell, and press Enter.

### The next 12 months

The most important part of the plan is the action list: what you will do, by when. Good actions are specific and small: "Raise SIP by 10% on 5 April", "Renew parents' health policy by 12 March with a super top-up", "File ITR by 15 July", "Family scam briefing at Onam".

### Share it

Show the plan to the people it affects: a spouse, parents, your money buddy. A plan that your family understands is a plan that survives a crisis.

## Local example

**Rahul's** one-page plan, at the end of the course (made-up numbers):

| Section | Rahul |
| --- | --- |
| Where I am | Net worth ₹2.9 lakh (liquid ₹96,000); take-home ₹30,600; savings rate 24% |
| Protection | Emergency fund ₹62,000 of ₹99,000 (3.8 months); Medisep for him and parents; term cover ₹25 lakh chosen, buying in January; PMSBY |
| Debt | Phone EMI cleared with arrears; sister's education loan as co-borrower from 2030; card paid in full monthly; report checked in May |
| Goals | Emergency fund by July; two-wheeler in 2028 (₹2,800/month RD); house decision in 2029 |
| Investing | IPS signed 4 November; contributory pension plus ₹1,500 SIP, +10% yearly; allocation 55/40/5 |
| Tax | New regime; tax ₹0 this year; ITR by 31 July; AIS check in June |
| Estate | Nominations checked September; will "after marriage"; money file with sister |
| Safety | Habits checklist done; family briefing at Onam |
| Income | Department exam for promotion in 2027 |
| Next 12 months | Term policy (Jan); emergency fund full (Jul); ITR (Jul); SIP step-up (Apr); yearly review (Nov) |

He printed it, put it on the inside of his cupboard door, and gave a copy to his sister.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [NCFE: free basic financial education course (e-LMS, about 5 hours)](https://ncfe.org.in/?p=430) | Optional revision: retake the NCFE course quizzes you found hardest | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Make a **Plan** tab with the template headings.
2. Link each number by formula from its tab, so it updates itself.
3. Write the short text parts: protection, debt plan, estate status, safety, income plan.
4. Write five to eight dated actions for the next 12 months and add them to your calendar.
5. Print or save the page as a PDF, and share it with the people it affects.

**Proof to record:** Your one-page plan (PDF or screenshot of the Plan tab, private numbers covered if you share it) and the calendar entries for its actions, saved in 17 Plan.

## Template: one-page plan (Plan tab)

```
MY FINANCIAL PLAN    Updated: ____
WHERE I AM: net worth ='Net Worth'!I4 | liquid ='Net Worth'!I7 | take-home ____ | savings rate ____%
PROTECTION: emergency fund =Emergency!B6 of =Emergency!B4 (=Emergency!B7 %) | life cover ____ | health cover ____ | accident ____
DEBT: total ____ | order ____ | debt-free by ____ | credit report checked on ____
GOALS (top 3): ____ ₹____ by ____ (₹____/month) | ____ | ____
INVESTING: IPS signed on ____ | allocation now __/__/__ vs target __/__/__ | contributions ₹____/month
TAX: regime ____ | expected tax ₹____ | ITR due ____
ESTATE: nominations checked ____ | will ____ | money file at ____ (who knows: ____)
SAFETY: habits checklist ____ | family briefing on ____
INCOME: 90-day plan ____ | result ____
NEXT 12 MONTHS: 1. ____ by ____  2. ____  3. ____  4. ____  5. ____
(Links: type = then click the other tab's cell; LibreOffice shows it as $'Sheet name'.A1)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Typing numbers into the plan by hand.** Link them, so the plan updates itself.
- **A plan with no dates.** Every action needs a month; put them in your calendar.
- **Keeping the plan secret.** Share it with the people it affects.
- **Waiting for perfect numbers.** A good plan now, improved yearly, beats a perfect plan never finished.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Why link the Plan tab's numbers by formula?
    - A) So the plan updates when the other tabs change
    - B) To hide the numbers
    - C) To make the file bigger
    - D) Because typing is not allowed
2. What is the most important part of the one-page plan?
    - A) The font
    - B) The colours
    - C) Last year's returns
    - D) The dated actions for the next 12 months
3. Which is a good action for the plan?
    - A) Invest wisely
    - B) Save more
    - C) Raise SIP by 10% on 5 April
    - D) Be better with money

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Optional revision of the NCFE quizzes you found hardest
- **Action:** Build your one-page plan with linked numbers and dated actions, and share it. It is done when your proof is saved: your one-page plan (PDF or screenshot of the Plan tab, private numbers covered if you share it) and the calendar entries for its actions, saved in 17 Plan.
- **Quiz:** at least 2 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** A plan that updates itself stays useful.
2. **D.** Actions with dates are what change your money.
3. **C.** It is specific and dated.

sections.title: FIN-M17-L03: The yearly money review: keeping the system running
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Run a complete yearly money review with a checklist, record it in a review log, and schedule your monthly, quarterly and yearly routines. **Time:** about 1 hour 30 minutes (15 minutes reading, 15 minutes resources, 60 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

A financial plan is not a document; it is a habit. Rules change, your life changes and markets move. A short yearly review keeps your plan true. Choose **one month** you will review every year (many people choose the month after their birthday, or April, when the tax year starts) and protect one weekend for it.

### The yearly review checklist

**Numbers**
1. Net worth and liquid net worth, compared with last year
2. A year of cash flow: income, spending, savings rate
3. Budget: categories that drifted; adjust the plan

**Protection**
4. Emergency fund: still the right size for this year's essential expenses?
5. Insurance: renewals, cover amounts (life, health for you and parents, accident, vehicle, home); any new dependants?
6. Free credit reports: download from a different bureau each time (FIN-M06-L04)

**Debt and goals**
7. Debts: progress against the payoff plan; any new debt and why
8. Goals: costs, dates and monthly savings updated; anything achieved, dropped or added

**Investing and retirement**
9. Allocation against the IPS; rebalance by rule
10. Retirement estimate recalculated; contributions stepped up
11. IPS reread; anything to change after a life event

**Tax and rules**
12. Tax regime choice for the new year; ITR due date and AIS check; advance tax if needed
13. Rule changes this year: the Union Budget (usually 1 February), small savings rates (every quarter), RBI decisions, SEBI and IRDAI changes; for Kerala government employees: DA orders, pension scheme news, Medisep renewal, GPF statement

**Estate and safety**
14. Nominations on every account; will; family money file updated
15. Family scam briefing; scam-proof habits checklist

**Income and next year**
16. Income growth: what worked, next 90-day test
17. The one-page plan updated, with next year's dated actions

### Smaller routines

- **Monthly (30 minutes):** the money review from the habits track: numbers, budget vs actual, one decision.
- **Quarterly (1 hour):** check small savings rates ([India Post](https://indiapost.gov.in/banking-services/saving)), your CAS ([AMFI](https://www.amfiindia.com/investor-corner/investor-center/cas.html)), AIS for TDS ([AIS](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/steps-to-access-ais-information-online)) and allocation drift.

### Keep a review log

One row per review: date, net worth, savings rate, the three biggest changes, and the decisions you made. In five years, this log will be the best record of how far you have come.

## Local example

**Fathima** chose November for her yearly review, because her freelance work is quieter then. Her first review, at the end of this course, took four hours over a weekend:

- Net worth up from −₹40,000 (her two-wheeler loan) a year ago to ₹1,85,000.
- Savings rate 26% on average, despite two slow months, thanks to the holding account.
- Rule changes she noted: new EPF withdrawal rules didn't affect her; NPS exit rules from December 2025 did; she reread them.
- Insurance: her mother's health policy renewed with a super top-up added; her own term cover deferred until marriage, with a note to revisit.
- Credit report: from a second bureau this time; clean.
- Decisions: raise PPF to ₹2,500 a month, keep the IPS unchanged, hold the family scam briefing at Christmas.

She added one row to her review log and booked the same weekend for next November.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [India Post: saving schemes and current interest rates](https://indiapost.gov.in/banking-services/saving) | The small savings rates to check every quarter | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03; check current rules |
| [AMFI: consolidated account statement (CAS)](https://www.amfiindia.com/investor-corner/investor-center/cas.html) | How to get your consolidated account statement for the review | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |
| [Income Tax Department: steps to access your Annual Information Statement (AIS)](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/steps-to-access-ais-information-online) | Opening your AIS before filing | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-03 |

## Action task (on your own money)

1. Choose your yearly review month and block a weekend in your calendar, repeating every year.
2. Add a **Review Log** to your Review tab with the template columns.
3. Do a first full yearly review now with the checklist (it is the end of your course year); write the first log row.
4. Put the monthly money date and the four quarterly checks in your calendar as repeating events.
5. Save the checklist in your Money Folder and on your phone.

**Proof to record:** Your first completed yearly review checklist, the first review log row and screenshots of the repeating calendar events, saved in 17 Plan.

## Template: yearly review checklist

```
YEARLY MONEY REVIEW    Date: ____
NUMBERS:      [ ] net worth  [ ] cash flow and savings rate  [ ] budget adjusted
PROTECTION:   [ ] emergency fund size  [ ] insurance renewals and cover  [ ] free credit report (bureau: ____)
DEBT, GOALS:  [ ] payoff progress  [ ] goals updated
INVESTING:    [ ] allocation vs IPS, rebalanced?  [ ] retirement recalculated, step-up done  [ ] IPS reread
TAX, RULES:   [ ] regime for the new year  [ ] ITR date and AIS  [ ] Budget and other rule changes noted
              [ ] (govt employee) DA, pension news, Medisep, GPF statement
ESTATE, SAFETY: [ ] nominations  [ ] will  [ ] money file  [ ] family scam briefing
INCOME:       [ ] last 90-day test result  [ ] next test
PLAN:         [ ] one-page plan updated with next year's dated actions
```

## Template: review log

```csv
Date,Net worth (₹),Liquid net worth (₹),Savings rate %,Emergency fund months,Debt (₹),Biggest changes this year,Decisions for next year
```

## Common mistakes

- **Reviewing only when things go wrong.** Fix the month in advance; regular reviews catch problems early.
- **Changing the IPS after a good or bad market year.** Change it for life events, not for market moods.
- **Ignoring rule changes.** Tax, savings rates and scheme rules change; note them every year.
- **Skipping the log.** The log turns years of small steps into visible progress.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. How often does the course suggest a full money review?
    - A) Every five years
    - B) Every day
    - C) Only when markets fall
    - D) Once a year, in a fixed month
2. When should you change your IPS?
    - A) After a friend's tip
    - B) After life events such as marriage, a job change or a big windfall
    - C) Every month
    - D) After every market fall
3. Which is a quarterly check in the course routine?
    - A) Small savings rates, CAS, AIS and allocation drift
    - B) Buying insurance
    - C) Writing a will
    - D) Changing your bank

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The quarterly check sources: India Post rates, the CAS and AIS
- **Action:** Schedule your routines, run your first yearly review and start the review log. It is done when your proof is saved: your first completed yearly review checklist, the first review log row and screenshots of the repeating calendar events, saved in 17 Plan.
- **Quiz:** at least 2 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** A fixed yearly review plus short monthly and quarterly checks.
2. **B.** The IPS follows your life, not market moods.
3. **A.** These change during the year and take an hour to check.

sections.summary: Retake the baseline self-assessment, compare your real money snapshot with your week 0 guesses, and check that every part of your plan exists.
sections.content:
Two things to finish the course: retake the baseline self-assessment, and check that every part of your plan exists.

## 1. Retake the self-assessment

Open the **Baseline** tab and fill in the **End** column for all 20 skills, without looking at your start scores first. Then compare:

- Which three skills grew the most? Write them in your one-page plan's notes.
- Any skill still at 1 or 2? Note which module covers it and plan one practice task for next month.
- Rewrite the **money snapshot** with real numbers now, next to your week 0 guesses. Where was your guess furthest from reality?

## 2. Check your toolkit

Each item should be a tab, a file or a note in your Money Folder that you could show a family member tomorrow. If something is missing, the module listed has its template.

| Toolkit item | Where the template is |
| --- | --- |
| Money Workbook with every tab filled in and dated | Week 0, used all course |
| Budget system: 30-day log, Budget tab with formulas, monthly routine | Module 3 |
| Net-worth tracker and cash-flow statement, updated this month | Module 2 |
| Emergency fund plan: target, where it is kept, monthly transfer, progress | Module 5 |
| Debt list with true costs, payoff plan and a checked credit report | Module 6 |
| Insurance checklist and a policy comparison done without buying | Module 7 |
| Investment Policy Statement, signed and dated | Modules 8, 9 and 17 |
| Tax checklist and the two-regime calculator | Module 10 |
| Goal funding plans and a retirement estimate | Modules 11 and 12 |
| Document register, nominations checked on every account, will decision | Module 13 |
| Scam-proof habits checklist, shared with your family | Module 15 |
| One-page financial plan and the yearly money-review checklist | Module 17 |

## Before you call the course done

- Save a backup of your progress from **Backup and courses** in this app, and keep it in your Money Folder.
- Download a copy of your Money Workbook (File → Download) and keep it offline too.
- Put your next monthly money date and your yearly review month in your calendar. The course ends; your money system doesn't.

sections.title: What next: your 12-month money routine
sections.summary: How to keep your money system running after the course: monthly, quarterly and yearly routines, life events, when to pay for advice and where to keep learning.
sections.content:
Finishing the course is the start of running your own money. Here is a sensible order for the next twelve months.

## Every month (30 minutes)

- The monthly money review on your money date: update the numbers, make one decision.
- Keep the 50/30/20 or zero-based budget you chose; log spending at least for one week each quarter, so you don't drift.

## Every quarter (1 hour)

- Small savings rates are announced every quarter: check if they changed ([India Post rates page](https://indiapost.gov.in/banking-services/saving)).
- Check your allocation against your Investment Policy Statement; rebalance only if it has drifted beyond your limits.
- Download your mutual fund and demat statement ([CAS](https://www.amfiindia.com/investor-corner/investor-center/cas.html)) and check that nominations and KYC show as complete.

## Every year (one weekend, in the same month every year)

Use the yearly money-review checklist from FIN-M17-L03: insurance renewals and cover, nominations, the will decision, the free credit reports, tax regime choice and ITR, goals and their timelines, and the one-page plan.

## When life changes, revisit these modules

| When this happens | Revisit |
| --- | --- |
| You get a Kerala government job | Module 14: the first-year plan, then Modules 7, 10 and 12 |
| You start freelancing or a business | FIN-M03-L04 and FIN-M10-L05, plus the Entrepreneurship course, Module 8 |
| Marriage or a child | Modules 7, 11 and 13: cover, goals and nominations |
| You plan to buy a house or vehicle | FIN-M11-L02 and FIN-M06-L03 |
| A big windfall: arrears, bonus, inheritance, sale of gold or land | Your Investment Policy Statement first, then Modules 8 and 9; wait 30 days before deciding |
| Someone offers a "great scheme" | Module 15, before you pay anything |

## When to pay for advice

You don't need an adviser to follow this course. Consider a fee-only SEBI-registered investment adviser when your investments become large or complicated, after a windfall, or before retirement. Check registration on the [SEBI list of registered investment advisers](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/other/OtherAction.do?doRecognisedFpi=yes&intmId=13) first, and read about fee limits in FIN-M09-L02. For tax notices or business accounts, use a chartered accountant.

## Keep learning, free

- [NCFE's free e-LMS course](https://ncfe.org.in/?p=430): about 5 hours on banking, insurance, pensions, investing and scams
- [Zerodha Varsity](https://zerodha.com/varsity/modules/): the Personal Finance, Mutual Funds, Insurance and NPS modules, read as education, not as product advice
- [OpenStax Principles of Finance](https://biz.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Finance/Principles_of_Finance_%28OpenStax%29): chapters 3, 7, 8, 15 and 20 for the theory behind interest, time value and risk
- [SEBI investor website](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/) and [RBI Financial Education](https://rbi.org.in/financialeducation/) for new rules and fraud warnings
- [NSE's free investor awareness programmes](https://www.nseindia.com/invest/investors-awareness-programs) (with study material) and [NISM's financial education programmes](https://www.nism.ac.in/financial-education); SEBI's Saa₹thi app for learning on your phone
- For Kerala government employees: the [Finance Department website](https://finance.kerala.gov.in/) for DA, pay and pension orders

## Keep up with rule changes

The Union Budget (usually on 1 February) can change tax rules; RBI changes rates through the year; Kerala announces DA and pay decisions by government order. Once a month, spend 15 minutes on the official pages linked in this course's sources log, and update your plan when something changes.

Every link on this page was checked on 2026-11-03; see the **Sources and verification log** for each one's status.

sections.title: Glossary with Malayalam meanings
sections.summary: 66 key personal finance terms in English and Malayalam, with simple meanings.
sections.content:
Key words from the course, roughly in the order you meet them. Many English words, such as EMI, SIP and KYC, are used as they are in Malayalam conversation; the Malayalam is given so you can explain them to family.

| English | മലയാളം (Malayalam) | Simple meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Budget** | ബജറ്റ് (വരവുചെലവ് പദ്ധതി) | A plan for how you will use the money you expect to receive |
| **Income** | വരുമാനം | Money you receive: salary, fees, business profit, interest |
| **Expense** | ചെലവ് | Money you spend |
| **Savings** | സമ്പാദ്യം | The part of income you don't spend |
| **Savings rate** | സമ്പാദ്യ നിരക്ക് | Savings as a percentage of income |
| **Needs and wants** | ആവശ്യങ്ങളും ആഗ്രഹങ്ങളും | What you must pay for, and what you would like to have |
| **Lifestyle inflation** | ജീവിതശൈലി ചെലവ് വർധന | Spending rising every time income rises, so saving never grows |
| **Asset** | ആസ്തി | Something you own that has money value |
| **Liability** | ബാധ്യത | Money you owe |
| **Net worth** | അറ്റ ആസ്തി | Everything you own minus everything you owe |
| **Cash flow** | പണമൊഴുക്ക് | Money coming in and going out over a period |
| **Emergency fund** | അടിയന്തര നിധി | Savings kept ready for job loss, illness or urgent repairs |
| **Inflation** | വിലക്കയറ്റം (പണപ്പെരുപ്പം) | Prices rising over time, so each rupee buys less |
| **Interest** | പലിശ | The price of borrowing money, or the reward for lending it |
| **Principal** | മുതൽ | The original amount borrowed or invested |
| **Compound interest** | കൂട്ടുപലിശ | Interest earned on earlier interest as well as on the principal |
| **EMI** | മാസത്തവണ (ഇ.എം.ഐ.) | Equated monthly instalment: a fixed monthly loan payment |
| **Loan** | വായ്പ | Money borrowed that must be repaid with interest |
| **Debt** | കടം | Money you owe to anyone |
| **Collateral** | ഈട് | Something pledged to a lender, such as gold, that can be taken if you don't repay |
| **Guarantor** | ജാമ്യക്കാരൻ | A person who promises to repay if the borrower doesn't |
| **Credit score** | ക്രെഡിറ്റ് സ്കോർ (വായ്പാ വിശ്വാസ്യത സ്കോർ) | A number that shows lenders how reliably you have repaid |
| **Savings account** | സേവിങ്സ് അക്കൗണ്ട് | A bank account for keeping money safely, with some interest |
| **Fixed deposit (FD)** | സ്ഥിര നിക്ഷേപം | A lump sum kept with a bank for a fixed time at a fixed rate |
| **Recurring deposit (RD)** | ആവർത്തന നിക്ഷേപം | A fixed amount deposited every month for a fixed time |
| **KYC** | ഉപഭോക്താവിനെ തിരിച്ചറിയൽ (കെ.വൈ.സി.) | Know Your Customer: proving your identity and address |
| **Nominee** | നോമിനി (നാമനിർദ്ദേശം ചെയ്യപ്പെട്ടയാൾ) | The person who receives the money in an account if you die |
| **Will** | വിൽപ്പത്രം | A written document saying who gets your property after you die |
| **Insurance** | ഇൻഷുറൻസ് | Paying a small, certain amount to be protected from a large, uncertain loss |
| **Premium** | പ്രീമിയം (ഇൻഷുറൻസ് തവണ) | The amount you pay for insurance |
| **Sum insured or sum assured** | ഇൻഷുറൻസ് തുക (പരിരക്ഷാ തുക) | The most the insurer will pay |
| **Claim** | ക്ലെയിം (നഷ്ടപരിഹാര അപേക്ഷ) | Asking the insurer to pay under your policy |
| **Term insurance** | ടേം ഇൻഷുറൻസ് (കാലാവധി ലൈഫ് ഇൻഷുറൻസ്) | Pure life cover for a fixed period, with no maturity payout |
| **Waiting period** | കാത്തിരിപ്പ് കാലയളവ് | Time after buying health cover before some illnesses are covered |
| **Investment** | നിക്ഷേപം | Putting money into something you expect to grow or pay income |
| **Risk** | നഷ്ടസാധ്യത (റിസ്ക്) | The chance that results differ from what you expect, including losses |
| **Return** | ആദായം (റിട്ടേൺ) | What an investment earns, as a percentage |
| **Real return** | യഥാർത്ഥ ആദായം | Return after subtracting inflation |
| **Asset allocation** | ആസ്തി വിന്യാസം | How your money is split between equity, debt, gold and cash |
| **Diversification** | വൈവിധ്യവൽക്കരണം | Spreading money across many investments so one failure hurts less |
| **Rebalancing** | പുനഃസന്തുലനം | Bringing your allocation back to its target |
| **Mutual fund** | മ്യൂച്വൽ ഫണ്ട് | A pool of many people's money invested by a professional manager |
| **SIP** | വ്യവസ്ഥാപിത നിക്ഷേപ പദ്ധതി (എസ്.ഐ.പി.) | Systematic investment plan: investing a fixed amount regularly |
| **NAV** | അറ്റ ആസ്തി മൂല്യം (എൻ.എ.വി.) | Net asset value: the price of one unit of a mutual fund |
| **Expense ratio** | ചെലവ് അനുപാതം | The yearly fee a fund takes, as a percentage of your money |
| **Index fund** | ഇൻഡക്സ് ഫണ്ട് (സൂചിക ഫണ്ട്) | A fund that simply copies a market index |
| **Share or stock** | ഓഹരി | A small part-ownership of a company |
| **Demat account** | ഡീമാറ്റ് അക്കൗണ്ട് | An account that holds shares and other securities electronically |
| **Dividend** | ലാഭവിഹിതം | Part of a company's or fund's profit paid to investors |
| **Capital gain** | മൂലധന നേട്ടം | Profit from selling an investment for more than you paid |
| **Income tax** | ആദായ നികുതി | Tax on your yearly income |
| **Tax regime** | നികുതി സമ്പ്രദായം | The set of rates and deductions you choose: old or new |
| **Deduction** | കിഴിവ് | An amount subtracted from income before tax is worked out |
| **TDS** | ഉറവിടത്തിൽ നികുതി പിടിക്കൽ (ടി.ഡി.എസ്.) | Tax deducted at source by the payer before paying you |
| **Income tax return (ITR)** | ആദായ നികുതി റിട്ടേൺ | The yearly statement of your income and tax filed with the department |
| **GST** | ചരക്ക് സേവന നികുതി (ജി.എസ്.ടി.) | Goods and Services Tax, charged on most sales of goods and services |
| **Provident fund** | പ്രൊവിഡന്റ് ഫണ്ട് (ഭാവിനിധി) | A long-term savings account for retirement, such as EPF, GPF or PPF |
| **Pension** | പെൻഷൻ | Regular income after retirement |
| **Dearness allowance (DA)** | ക്ഷാമബത്ത | An allowance added to pay to offset rising prices |
| **Retirement corpus** | വിരമിക്കൽ നിധി | The total savings you need to live on after you stop working |
| **Chitty** | ചിട്ടി (കുറി) | A group saving and borrowing scheme where members bid for the monthly prize |
| **Co-operative society** | സഹകരണ സംഘം | A member-owned organisation; some take deposits, but not all are licensed banks |
| **Ponzi scheme** | പോൻസി തട്ടിപ്പ് | A fraud that pays old investors with new investors' money until it collapses |
| **Phishing** | ഫിഷിങ് (വ്യാജ സന്ദേശ തട്ടിപ്പ്) | Fake messages or sites that trick you into giving passwords or OTPs |
| **Investment Policy Statement** | നിക്ഷേപ നയരേഖ | Your written rules for investing: goals, allocation, what you will and won't do |
| **Financial plan** | സാമ്പത്തിക പദ്ധതി | Your goals and the steps, numbers and dates to reach them |

sections.title: Sources and verification log
sections.summary: Every link in the course, where it is used and when it was checked (2026-11-03).
sections.content:
Every link in this course is listed here with the date it was checked. Links were opened and read on 2026-11-03; nothing here was copied from memory. If a link stops working, search for its title on the same website.

- **verified 2026-11-03:** the page was opened on that date and its content matched what the course says.
- **verified 2026-11-03; check current rules:** as above, but it is a rate, limit or rule that changes often. Open the source before you act.
- **verified 2026-11-03 (headline checked):** the page could not be opened in full, so only its headline and date were checked in a web search. The course uses it only for what the headline itself says.
- **unverified:** the site blocks automated checks, so the page could not be opened for this course. The address is the official one named by other government sources; type it yourself and check that it is the real site.

Government and regulator pages are preferred. Where an official page could not be opened or doesn't exist in plain text, a dated news report or a bank's official page is used instead, and its date is in the title. OpenStax *Principles of Finance* is licensed CC BY 4.0, and this course only links to it.
